{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Budget Constraint Made Into Style","laconic":"Economic scarcity read as the film's governing aesthetic logic.","note":"Each reading treats a film's material poverty — small frame, two-man cast, microbudget — not as limitation but as the organizing formal principle. The economy of production becomes the text's signature.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Maker Who Loved His Killing Machine As Son","laconic":"Dante's warbeast is his disowned, monstrous offspring.","note":"Four readings circle the same code: a creator whose engineered weapon is a displaced child — authored, named, loved, mourned. The machine externalizes its maker's death drive and parental failure.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Heathcliff As Britain's Returning Slave-Trade Ghost","laconic":"The outsider read as the empire's disavowed colonial wealth made flesh.","note":"These readings recast Heathcliff and his return as the repressed colonial economy of slavery come back to claim the house. The casting-debate reading belongs as the meta-version of the same national amnesia.","members":[0,1,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Eye That Wounds Itself For Looking","laconic":"Scopophilia turned self-punishing — sight becomes the crime and its blinding sentence.","note":"Each reading frames looking as transgression that recoils on the watcher, whether through a blindfolded gaze, a wound of watching, or blindness as penalty. The desire to see is inseparable from the punishment for seeing.","members":[0,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Bird As Externalized Psyche","laconic":"Birds incarnate the protagonist's split-off interior — spirit, repression, rage.","note":"Each reading treats the bird not as creature but as a projection of some interior force—superego, repression, maternal rage, tutelary spirit—externalized into flight. The code is the avian as exteriorized psyche.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Hoax That Indicts the Market That Bought It","laconic":"Mr. Brainwash's sudden success exposes art as speculative bubble, not aesthetics.","note":"Every reading treats Mr. Brainwash not as artist but as symptom — the manufactured phenomenon (auction boom, capital, literary forgery, the queue) that reveals the market's hunger to validate anything. The code is the prank-as-critique: the fraud certifies the system it parodies.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Wounded Child Inside The Gentle Man","laconic":"Rogers's tenderness reread as a frightened child speaking through puppets.","note":"All three recast Fred Rogers's warmth as the survival strategy of a scared inner child, projected outward through puppetry and one-to-one address. The code is the adult ministry as the displaced voice of his own wound.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Daughter Effaced By The Father's Name","laconic":"Patriarchal genius consumes the daughter into nothing.","note":"Both readings frame Adèle as a self annihilated by the gravitational weight of the paternal name and reputation. The father's authority operates as both colonial apparatus and economy of genius, leaving the daughter erased.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Border Between Body And Machine Dissolves","laconic":"Films staking everything on collapsing the organic/mechanical or human/nonhuman line.","note":"Each reading locates the film's core on a dividing border—pre-human, cyborg, organic/mechanical—and asserts that border is the true subject, or is being erased.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Aspect Ratio As Streaming-Era Argument","laconic":"Frame shape becomes a polemic about cinema in the algorithm's living room.","note":"Each reading treats the deliberate frame—square, 65mm, expanding, restaged formats—as a self-conscious statement made against or within the streaming context. The code is the frame-as-thesis, the image arguing about its own conditions of viewing.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Stolen Name That Devours Its Wearer","laconic":"Assuming another's identity becomes a self-annihilating possession.","note":"In each, a borrowed or invented name overtakes the man who adopts it — the alias eats its wearer, whether brother, actor, or terrorist-as-brand.","members":[0,3,4,5]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Frontier As Enclosure Of The Commons","laconic":"American origins read as the quiet liquidation of shared land.","note":"Each reading frames the American frontier not as discovery but as theft — the privatization of a commons (the cow, the trees) as the nation's original sin. A genuine recurring interpretive move, not a vague theme.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Bond That Hallucinates the Other Across Space","laconic":"Two souls fuse into one telepathic, mutually-imagined object.","note":"Each reading treats the Force-bond as a shared hallucination collapsing two beings into a single divided self. The dyad becomes a literal apparatus of transference between split halves of one soul.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Kite As Severed Mandate","laconic":"The kite as fragile tether to a vanishing heaven.","note":"Both readings cast the kite as a binding cord—mandate, tether—that history snaps. The shared code is the kite as a doomed line of continuity.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Frozen Frame Of Muybridge's Motion Study","laconic":"Cinema arrested into the serial stillness of chronophotography.","note":"Each reading invokes the freeze-frame or serialized pose as a descendant of Muybridge's motion studies, reading movement as a sequence of arrested instants. The film's flow is decomposed into the tableau, the strike, the frozen gallop.","members":[0,1,2,3,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Alphabet As Engine Of Power","laconic":"Language itself becomes the apparatus that builds law and prison.","note":"Each reading treats the alphabet not as transparent medium but as machinery — constructing moral history, ontology, or carceral order. The code makes letters the load-bearing structure of power.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Etiquette Mistaken For Ethics","laconic":"Manners impersonate morality; politeness becomes the mask power wears.","note":"Each reading exposes civility as a substitute for ethics — courtesy that suspends confrontation, launders racism, or disguises decay. The code is the strikingly recurrent move of treating manners as the thing they only pretend to be: virtue.","members":[0,1,2,3,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The White Settler Who Won't Leave Africa","laconic":"Colonial inheritors clinging to a land already refusing them.","note":"These readings frame white protagonists whose belonging in Africa is a fiction outliving its expiry. Maria Vial and the Tabu colonial each cling to a possession the land has revoked.","members":[1,2,3]},{"name":"The Migrant Who Discovers Her Welcome Was Her Wage","laconic":"Hospitality unmasked as exploitation across the colonial threshold.","note":"This reading inverts the settler perspective — the colonized servant brought into the metropole, whose belonging is only a transaction. Distinct enough from the African-settler cluster to stand alone.","members":[4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Western Prize As Foreign Verdict","laconic":"European festival laurels read as the West judging Asian cinema's worth.","note":"Each reading treats a Berlin or Venice award not as recognition but as an interpretive act — the West absolving, indulging, sparing, or vindicating what the films' own cultures contest. The prize becomes a verdict that overrides domestic judgment.","members":[0,1,3,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Director's Real House As Set","laconic":"An actual dwelling—often the filmmaker's own—becomes the diegetic home.","note":"Each reading locates meaning in a real house pressed into fiction: the filmmaker's own, inherited, or childhood home collapsing the boundary between lived space and set. The charge comes from authenticity bleeding into the frame.","members":[0,3,4,5,6]},{"name":"The Real Horror House As Pilgrimage","laconic":"Filming on the genre's actual landmark house fuses dread with tourism.","note":"Both readings stage their action at a real horror-cinema house, where shooting on hallowed ground turns murder into a kind of location pilgrimage.","members":[1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Altar That Eats Its Devotees","laconic":"Mastery as a deity demanding flesh and blood in tribute.","note":"Each reading recasts pursuit—of art, of greatness, of wealth—as a sacrificial cult whose god feeds on the worshipper. The vocation is literalized as religion with a body count.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Village That Is Not Where It Stands","laconic":"Filmed villages as fictions: imagined, impossible, or visually sealed off.","note":"Each reading treats the on-screen village as a constructed elsewhere — a postcard for a nonexistent place, a real coast standing in for an imagined city, a settlement deprived of sky. The locale is a fabrication, not a documentary fact.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Man Disowned For The Myth","laconic":"Arthur repudiates the icon the crowd loves; they wanted the symbol.","note":"Each Joker reading turns on the rupture between the suffering man and the symbol projected onto him — Arthur, Lee, and the audience all preferring the myth to the person. The film names this co-delusion as its own subject.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Smile As The Murder Weapon","laconic":"Affability is not the mask but the violence itself.","note":"Each reading collapses the distance between geniality and atrocity, insisting the warm grin is not a disguise over cruelty but its very instrument. The pleasant surface does the killing.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Capital As A Devouring God","laconic":"Wealth reimagined as an insatiable deity demanding worship and sacrifice.","note":"Each reading recasts capital not as economic system but as ravenous divinity — a hoard, a hunger, a cross-wearing spirit, an eschatology. The recurring move is theologizing money into something that consumes the worshipper.","members":[0,1,2,3,5,6]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Distributor's Cut As Confession","laconic":"American re-edits betray what the studio system feared.","note":"Each reading treats the mutilated American release print not as vandalism but as an inadvertent ideological confession — the cut itself becomes the text, exposing distrust of slowness, fuse-tension, dream-logic, or memory.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Riviera As Painted Unreality","laconic":"The Mediterranean coast read as canvas, not geography.","note":"Each reading treats the Côte d'Azur not as a real place but as a heightened aesthetic surface — a painterly edge where landscape becomes pure cinematic artifice.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Field Read Through Van Gogh","laconic":"Cinematic landscape framed as a Van Gogh canvas.","note":"Each invokes Van Gogh's brush to recode an image — the sunflower field, the worn boots — into painterly transfiguration. The shared move is reading film frames as Van Gogh paintings.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Invented Self Made Real By Performance","laconic":"A fabricated persona becomes the true self through enactment.","note":"Each reading treats an assumed identity not as disguise but as a speech-act that constitutes a new self, displacing or killing the original. The Hit Man and Primal Fear cases share the same Bloomian misreading: performance precedes and produces being.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}
{"verdict":"reject","groups":[]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Camera Seated At The Table","laconic":"Cooking filmed in real time turns viewer into fellow diner.","note":"Both readings treat unfaked culinary labor as a device that collapses the distance between screen and spectator, making the camera a participant rather than a witness.","members":[0,1]},{"name":"Intimacy Improvised At A Shared Table","laconic":"Real tables and unscripted moments manufacture on-set closeness.","note":"Here the device is the literal table as a generator of improvised intimacy between actors, the meal staged as a method for producing unrehearsed connection.","members":[2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Stateless Cinema Funding Its Own Sovereignty","laconic":"National films read as acts of financial and formal self-determination.","note":"Each reading treats production conditions—who pays, who exiles, who refuses—as the political grammar of an unrecognized or compromised national cinema. The money is the meaning.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Flop Reborn As Sacred Object","laconic":"Films that failed in theaters, then were recanonized through afterlife circulation.","note":"Each reading locates meaning not in the text but in its reception arc — the gap between initial commercial verdict and later cultural sanctification. The code reads the film through its own marketing and afterlife.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Dostoevsky's Underground Man Walks Among Us","laconic":"The spiteful, paralyzed diarist reincarnated in modern milieus.","note":"Each reading transplants Dostoevsky's Underground Man (or his cousin Oblomov) into a contemporary or unexpected setting — the snow, the convenience store, the cab, the marketing polo. The code is the recognition of that specific resentful, inert consciousness wearing new clothes.","members":[0,1,4,5]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Critical Verdict As Cultural Symptom","laconic":"Critics' dismissals read as confessions of a culture's lost literacies.","note":"Each reading flips the critical reception into evidence: the mockery, the 'confusing' verdict, the 'middlebrow' label all become symptoms of an audience that can no longer read allegory or the reading life. The device indicts the critic, not the film.","members":[0,1,2,3,4,5]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Dead Who Narrate Mexico","laconic":"An omniscient voice catalogs the nation's casualties beside the living plot.","note":"Both films summon a Rulfian register where the murmuring dead and the offscreen body count haunt the foreground story. Mexico itself is narrated as a country of ghosts the characters cannot hear.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Critics Praised What Let Them Off","laconic":"Acclaim as the very evasion the film indicts.","note":"Each reading reframes critical praise as complicit: the rave performs the blindness, forgiveness, or self-flattery the film was quietly diagnosing. The applause becomes evidence for the prosecution.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Missing Bridge Is The Point","laconic":"The structural gap, the absent transition, becomes the work's true subject.","note":"Each reading locates meaning in a film's refusal to connect halves — the unbridged break between movements is not a flaw but the thesis. The diptych structure forces the viewer to supply, or mourn, the vanished middle.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Surface That Has No Depth","laconic":"All gleam, no interior — the film as pure advertised exterior.","note":"Each reading insists the film is depthless by design: surface, commercial, shallow-canonized, an empty superlative. They converge on one code — the work that means nothing beneath its own polish, and triumphs precisely there.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Arizona Standing In For The Mythic West","laconic":"The frontier shot in a place that isn't the frontier.","note":"Each reading locates the Western (or its refusal) in Arizona/Tucson backlots and reads the substitution as exposing the frontier myth as constructed terrain.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Domestic Labor That Carries Grief","laconic":"Mundane motion masks the family's buried cruelty and mourning.","note":"Both readings locate the film's engine in the home's relentless small acts—the mother's quiet cruelty and the ceaseless hands of cooking and care. They share a code: domestic routine as the vessel and concealment of unresolved grief.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Costume That Speaks What The Self Cannot","laconic":"Disguise as confession; the mask voices the truth the face suppresses.","note":"Each reading frames costume not as concealment but as the only vessel for an unbearable truth — tenderness, mourning, guilt, impotence smuggled in through borrowed skin.","members":[0,1,2,3,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Tear That Decodes The Film","laconic":"A single weeping becomes the key to the whole.","note":"Each reading elevates one moment of crying into a master cipher that unlocks the film's buried meaning. The tear is not emotion but interpretation made visible.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Symbolic Order Fails To Hold","laconic":"Authority collapses when its symbolic guarantee no longer slots the subject.","note":"Each reading diagnoses a breakdown in symbolic authority—the paternal/social code that assigns place and law. Whether through possession, witchcraft, arrested manhood, or virginal exclusion, the subject confronts an order that has lost its anchoring power.","members":[1,2,3,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Friend As Means, Not End","laconic":"Friendship weaponized: the beloved face reduced to instrument or betrayal.","note":"These readings turn friendship into a moral test of treating the other as means versus end. Waymond's kindness-as-ethic and Lightfoot's last-good-thing both invert the cynicism, but all five orbit the same code: the friend's face as the site where instrumental use meets fatal intimacy.","members":[0,1,2,3,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Sacred Island That Could Not Be Filmed","laconic":"Iwo Jima as forbidden body, conjured from elsewhere.","note":"Both readings treat the island as a sacralized, unfilmable body — the Emperor's flesh turned inside out, a ground too holy to shoot, summoned from Iceland and a quarry. The island is less location than relic.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"Spielberg Atones For His Own Spectacle","laconic":"The maker repents the wonder-machine he built.","note":"These readings frame Spielberg's prestige works as self-indictments — monochrome and carnage offered as penance for the spectacle he himself invented.","members":[4,6]},{"name":"The Movie Brats Rebel Against The Auteur Seventies","laconic":"Blockbuster craft staged as revolt against arthouse seriousness.","note":"Each reads an entertainment as a counterstroke — painted antiquity, pulp adventure, manufactured wonder — against the auteurist or effects-driven culture it answered.","members":[2,3,5]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Demimonde Doubles The Boardroom","laconic":"Nightlife spaces read as mirrors of corporate-economic power.","note":"Each reading stages a marginal or pleasure space (club, banlieue underworld, champagne room) as the secret double or smuggled-in twin of legitimate institutional power. The trope insists the underworld and the tower share one architecture.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Dissolve As Death And Dissolution","laconic":"The lap-dissolve read as the visible form of vanishing and death.","note":"These readings treat the cinematic dissolve (or its figural cousins—dissolving walls, a puddle) as the death drive or dissolution of the subject made visible. The optical transition becomes a theory of disappearance.","members":[0,1,2,3,4]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Interchangeable Room As Stateless Limbo","laconic":"Identical chambers dissolve nation, marking power's placeless, post-historical zone.","note":"These readings find in the fungible luxe interior a figure for sovereignty unmoored from territory — the room that could be anywhere is the world after borders. The repetition of 'interchangeable' is the code's signature.","members":[0,3,4]},{"name":"The Threshold Room As Border Regime","laconic":"An institutional interior enforces the partition it pretends to neutralize.","note":"The sewer and the break room each become the true cartography of a divided Europe — a transit space recoded as the site where boundaries are policed and revealed.","members":[1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Spectacle Dismissed Is The Argument","laconic":"'Dumb spectacle' verdicts miss that spectacle was the whole point.","note":"Each reading flips the genre-snob complaint: what critics dismiss as mere spectacle is itself the film's thesis and meaning. The dismissal becomes evidence of misreading.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Christmas As Commodity Masking Its Violence","laconic":"The holiday's cheer industrially manufactured, concealing cruelty beneath festive packaging.","note":"Each reading treats Christmas not as sentiment but as a production machine—Santa suits, assembly lines, canonized classics—that processes and hides violence inside the commodity of cheer. The activated expectation is warmth; the code exposes the cruelty the wrapping conceals.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Witch Is What Naming Makes Her","laconic":"To call a woman witch is to conjure the power feared.","note":"Both films locate witchcraft not in the supernatural but in the social act of designation — the accusation creates the very power it claims to detect.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The City Assembled From Elsewhere","laconic":"Named places are composites stitched from foreign, fabricated, or impossible sites.","note":"Each reading exposes a setting whose nominal location is a fiction built from other places — palaces that never touch, a real facade fronting a fabricated interior, a city that is really a soundstage. The code is the place that exists only as montage.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Love Built On Asymmetric Power Over Her","laconic":"Romance reframed as the lover's unilateral control over a consentless woman.","note":"Each reading exposes the romantic male position as one of unequal power — purchasing, deleting, rewinding, or surveilling a partner who cannot truly consent. The beloved is rendered an object whose autonomy is structurally erased by the lover's apparatus.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The World Already Dead Before Death","laconic":"Life as posthumous condition the protagonist alone hasn't registered.","note":"Both readings posit a reality already extinguished, with death merely a delayed acknowledgment of a prior cessation. The living move through a corpse-world they cannot name.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Severed Sacred Head As Looted Nation","laconic":"A decapitated Buddha figures the plundered body of the postcolonial state.","note":"Both readings cast the stolen Buddha head as synecdoche for a nation dismembered by looting, repatriation its phantom-limb ache. Index 0 invokes a corpse and Catholic modernity, not a severed sacred relic.","members":[1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Body Wounded As Performance Art","laconic":"Self-destruction staged as artwork upon one's own flesh.","note":"These readings frame bodily endangerment and self-disfigurement as deliberate aesthetic acts — the wound becomes the work, the performance is the harm done to oneself.","members":[0,1,4,5,7,8]},{"name":"The Anarchist Whose Violence Is Theatre","laconic":"Destruction of meaning and order as public spectacle.","note":"Both figures stage their nihilist or anarchist violence as theatrical performance, attacking signification and authority through curated public acts.","members":[2,9]},{"name":"The Disciple Who Murdered To Become The Icon","laconic":"Killing the master, or one's own image, as authorship.","note":"These two cast the act of destroying an icon — even one's own — as a transfer or seizure of mythic identity.","members":[3,6]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Keepsake That Betrays Its Memory","laconic":"The souvenir preserves the love by falsifying it.","note":"Both readings treat the title-object as a relic that outlives the relationship yet distorts what it claims to keep, making memory and counterfeit inseparable.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Self Priced on an Open Market","laconic":"Human worth recast as line-item bid in a transactional ledger.","note":"Both readings expose a covert pricing mechanism beneath ostensibly personal choices — romance or solidarity reframed as auction, where the person becomes a quantified asset. The 'hidden ontology' move locates value not in feeling but in market calculus.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Samurai Code Exposed As Hollow Performance","laconic":"Honor reread as empty ritual masking absence of meaning.","note":"Each reading treats the warrior's code—duty, honor, the Symbolic Order itself—as a brittle performance whose collapse reveals nihilism underneath. The figures eat, sacrifice, or kill having already renounced the very ideals they enact.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Film Run On Video-Game Logic","laconic":"Narrative governed by respawn, save files, and console ontology.","note":"Each reading decodes the film as structured by gaming's machinery—death-and-retry loops, save states, the logic of the console—rather than conventional dramatic causality.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Festival Crowns A National Anxiety","laconic":"Prizes awarded less for cinema than for what a nation needs to confess.","note":"Each reading reframes a major award (Palme, critical canonization) as a political act: the West or France crowning a film because it externalizes an anxiety about migrants, outsiders, or itself. The prize becomes a mirror, not a measure of cinema.","members":[0,1,3,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Fairy Tale Priced And Notarized","laconic":"Cinderella reread as a transaction, romance disclosed as terms.","note":"Both readings strip the rescue-romance to its ledger: love arrives as a contract, the fairy tale exposed as a negotiated price. The enchantment is the deal.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Ship of Theseus Replaces Its Parts","laconic":"Identity as continual substitution until no original remains.","note":"Both readings deploy the Theseus paradox as a code for a self whose components are silently swapped, leaving no fixed core. One stages it biologically as cellular refraction, the other as a body literally rebuilt from donated organs.","members":[0,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Patient Camera As Painter Of Light","laconic":"Slowness reframed as painterly stillness; duration becomes composition.","note":"Both readings convert narrative patience into a pictorial idiom, casting the held shot as a painter's arrangement of light. The recurring move equates cinematic slowness with painting, charging stillness with composed expectation.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Dead Time As Filmic Truth","laconic":"Loose method yields lived, unhurried duration onscreen","note":"Both readings locate authenticity in production constraint—improvisation or one-take economy—that produces dead time as documentary-grade truth of presence.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Violence And Dance As One Geometry","laconic":"Motion read as choreography, whether killing or courtship.","note":"Each reading collapses the line between fighting and dancing, treating bodily motion as a single continuous geometric language. The gunfight is a pirouette; the dance is a mathematics of unbroken movement.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Last Keeper Of A Dying Cinema","laconic":"Custodians tending the apparatus as the medium itself expires.","note":"Each reading personifies cinema's death through a lone caretaker bound to failing machinery or vanishing rites. The projector, the empty hall, the aging cinephile all figure film mourning itself.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Showman Who Trades In Your Gaze","laconic":"The barker-impresario whose true commodity is the spectator's own attention.","note":"Each reading reframes a performer-figure as a carnival barker monetizing the audience's complicity—selling them their own watching. The devil-host counting viewers, the venture-capitalist hustler, the address to the spectator, and the impresario peddling his star all stage the showman as broker of the gaze.","members":[0,1,3,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Mediocrity That Recognizes Genius It Lacks","laconic":"Salieri's wound: to see brilliance one can name but never possess.","note":"Each reading frames a watcher who comprehends greatness precisely because he is barred from achieving it — the connoisseur of a gift denied him. The recurring 'Salieri' invocation makes this an explicit, activated code of envious recognition.","members":[1,3]},{"name":"The Prodigy Who Fled His Own Gift","laconic":"Talent so vast its bearer flees rather than wields it.","note":"These read the gifted one who burns, buries, or runs from mastery — the opposite pole from the envious witness. The drama is refusal of one's own power, not longing for another's.","members":[0,2]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"Shot In Order So Decay Felt Real","laconic":"Chronological filming as engine of lived, discovered emotion.","note":"These readings credit sequential shooting itself with producing emotion the actors seem to discover rather than perform — betrayal and despair earned in narrative time.","members":[1,2]},{"name":"The Camera That Could Not Stop","laconic":"Documentary nerve: the lens kept rolling past the safe point.","note":"Both readings fix on a camera implicated by its refusal to look away — danger captured because filming continued past where it should have stopped.","members":[0,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Canonization As The Culture's Self-Absolution","laconic":"A film's enshrinement exposes the era's need to forgive or sanctify itself.","note":"Each reading treats the act of canonizing a film as a symptom — the culture elevates a work to launder its own anxieties, whether about informers, therapeutic confession, or wartime guilt. [0] names the anxiety bare; [1],[2],[3] each diagnose what a specific enshrinement absolves.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Saint Who Starves To Author Her Flesh","laconic":"Self-starvation as sacred rebellion, the body refused into holiness.","note":"A recurring code where female hunger becomes mystic authorship — fasting reframed as sanctity, resistance, and control over one's own disappearing flesh.","members":[1,2,3,4,5,6,7]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Number Title As Hidden Deadline","laconic":"Numerals in the title encode a temporal sentence, not a label.","note":"Each reading treats a numeric title as a coded expiration — a birthdate-as-deadline, a year constancy ends, an unrentable number. The figure smuggles time's verdict into what looks like neutral notation.","members":[0,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Old Warship Towed To Its Death","laconic":"Turner's painting as elegy for obsolete glory awaiting scrap.","note":"Both readings load the same image: Turner's Téméraire as a code for a fading order—empire, the analog hero—dragged off by the new. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Artwork That Names Its Own Film","laconic":"The film titles itself after the burning image it depicts.","note":"Both readings collapse the distance between the painting inside the film and the film as object — the burning dress and the painting's title each become the work in miniature, a mise en abyme of self-naming.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Republic That Voted Its Own Death","laconic":"Democracy as the lawful machinery of its own abolition.","note":"These readings see democratic procedure not as bulwark but as the very instrument of tyranny's birth — the vote, the applause, the manufactured crisis that hands power away. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Title Is The Verb 'To Return'","laconic":"Each reading reads a film through its return-naming title.","note":"All four interpret the film by parsing its title's act of returning — round-trip versus homecoming, the dead's return, the changed returner. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Recording That Judges Its Speaker","laconic":"Playback and archive indict the self that listens back.","note":"Tape, archive, and confession become instruments that measure or condemn a vanishing self. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Hero Forbidden To Die","laconic":"Bond's immortality reframed as curse; his death the franchise's only honest act.","note":"These readings converge on franchise eternity as a tyranny, and Bond's death as the rupture that exposes our faith in his endlessness. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Sport That Eats Its Disposable Bodies","laconic":"Spectacle as forced labour grinding expendable underclass flesh.","note":"Each reading frames athletic or gladiatorial spectacle as a machine consuming the bodies of the disposable — labourers, prisoners, the provincial poor — for entertainment or profit. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Pacific Northwest Wilderness As Lost Eden","laconic":"Oregon's forests filmed as a paradisal margin pressing against the city.","note":"Each reading treats a real Pacific Northwest landscape as a semi-sacred wilderness — Eden, pilgrimage site, or refuge — set in tension with urban encroachment. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Asylum As Mind Externalized","laconic":"Madness projected outward into architecture and disavowed authority.","note":"Each reading treats the asylum or its framing as the psyche made spatial — repression rendered as building, the doctor as projected aggression, the frame as disciplinary enclosure. {"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"Gold Smuggled Out Through Imperial Plumbing","laconic":"Heists that move bullion against the currency-controls of a fading empire.","note":"Both films read theft as a circumvention of postwar austerity and exchange restrictions — the loot is the empire's own gold, repatriated by larceny. {"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Lip-Reader As Surveillance Apparatus","laconic":"Reading mouths becomes the cinema's confession of its own spying.","note":"These readings make the act of decoding silent speech into an allegory of the surveillance state and the camera's voyeurism. {"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Narrator Who Sees Beyond The Body","laconic":"Voiceover overflows its possible vantage, exposing desire or spectacle as the true speaker.","note":"Both readings treat impossible omniscience not as convention but as a force—desire, spectacle—usurping the diegesis. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Léaud The Actor As His Own Ghost","laconic":"Jean-Pierre Léaud's body read as living archive of itself.","note":"Both readings treat Léaud not as a character but as a persona haunted by his own performing history—mortality and self-reference fused in the actor's flesh.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Ancient War Built On A Soundstage","laconic":"Epic riverine battles revealed as fabricated studio constructions.","note":"Both readings expose the grand historical battlefield as an artifice of backlot and soundstage, foregrounding the manufactured nature of cinematic war spectacle.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Salvaged Body Driven Toward Home","laconic":"The amputee-machine reassembled, steering wreckage back toward a lost origin.","note":"Furiosa's prosthetic arm and Fury Road's hybrid bodies read the missing limb as salvage, the surviving body as machine, and motion as return.","members":[0,4,5]},{"name":"The Lost Limb As Insurgent Remainder","laconic":"A withered or interchangeable limb encodes systemic reason or revolt.","note":"Here the limb is not salvage-toward-home but a sign of surplus and instrumental logic—revolutionary remainder in Lagaan, technocratic prosthesis in Enter the Dragon.","members":[1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Camera That Refuses To Cut Away","laconic":"Horror earned by holding the practical body in frame.","note":"Each reading locates dread not in suggestion but in the unflinching, tactile presence of the made body — gore, prosthetic, transformation — that the film insists we watch.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Postwar Threshold That Re-Sorts The Returning Man","laconic":"Counter, fountain, back door — sites where peace redistributes who was promised what.","note":"Each reading turns a domestic threshold into the machinery of postwar reabsorption, where the soldier or citizen is quietly re-ranked by class, race, or economy. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Neutrality Is The Choice That Cannot Be Made","laconic":"Each film exposes neutrality as a fiction the burning world annuls.","note":"These readings share a single semiotic move: the refusal to take sides is unmasked as itself a fatal choice. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Life Rewritten As Inscription","laconic":"Biography refused; the woman exists only as text, composition, writing.","note":"Each reading insists the film does not depict a life but constructs one through the act of writing or composition, denying its female subject a conventional 'story.' {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Hospitality That Outranks The Law","laconic":"The defenceless face commands welcome beyond, even against, legality.","note":"Each reading stages a Levinasian ethics where the stranger's face imposes an obligation that overrides law, even justifying trespass or transgression. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Sex Worker Who Authored Her Own Image","laconic":"Maxine converts stigma into self-made stardom, refusing the victim's script.","note":"All four read Maxine's arc as a porn performer seizing authorship over her image — branding the stigma as marquee, refusing the Lovelace-victim role. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Dirt as the Visible Mark of Class","laconic":"Filth made literal so the class border can be seen.","note":"Each reading converts 'dirt' from grime into a semiotic boundary marker, the body and earth staining the lower order against the gentry. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Crown Backdated To Steal Neorealism","laconic":"Origin-myth as theft: priority claims that erase rivals and inconvenient roots.","note":"Both readings treat 'first neorealist' as a contested crown awarded by backdating, with the coronation suppressing what came before or what the film actually was. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Foreign City Faked On English Soundstages","laconic":"American/comic metropolis conjured from British studio backlots.","note":"Both readings catch the same code: an iconic transatlantic cityscape constructed on English soil, its 'authenticity' a continental sleight of hand. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Island That Plays A Lost World","laconic":"Hawaiian landscape cast as Eden, prehistory, or warzone — always somewhere already fallen.","note":"Each reading turns a real Pacific island into a stage for a vanished or doomed elsewhere, where the location's lush beauty is precisely what marks it as a ruin-in-waiting. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Survival That Refuses Its Grief","laconic":"Tending the living masks a wound left unmourned.","note":"Both readings locate trauma in a devotion or persistence that substitutes for mourning, the buried wound sustained rather than released. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The English Address Wearing Another Realm's Face","laconic":"British architecture cast as the seat of foreign or vanishing power.","note":"Each reading turns a real London or Georgian location into a stand-in for an empire, regime, or facade — the building itself becomes a mask. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Child Forced To Carry The World","laconic":"Childhood collapsed under adult burdens it should never bear.","note":"These readings share one code: the child who is aged, indicted, or yoked to a weight beyond his years — innocence conscripted into the labor of survival, witness, or judgment. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Pastoral As America's Comforting Lie","laconic":"Idyllic landscape exposed as a fragile or false national promise.","note":"Each reading turns a rural American vista into an ideology — a pastoral myth that either deceives or fails to protect. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Forced Perspective As Worldview Made Visible","laconic":"A spatial trick becomes the film's moral and ideological lens.","note":"Each reading treats forced perspective not as mere spectacle but as a device that renders a stance toward existence visible — pinning, fabricating, or ideologically warping its world. The shared code is the optical distortion read as worldview.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Color Wielded As An Authorial Signature","laconic":"Color stops being decor and becomes the maker's deliberate hand.","note":"Each reading treats color not as mood but as a self-conscious authorial instrument — the editor's pencil, the director's perceptual quirk, the cinematographer's character. The shared code is color-as-signature, color that announces its own authorship.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Body As Articulated Philosophy","laconic":"The martial artist whose physical technique IS a stated doctrine.","note":"Each reading reframes fighting prowess as theorized philosophy made flesh — the body as argument, not spectacle. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The City Worn As Disguise","laconic":"Real cities filmed as stand-ins, cages, or contraband.","note":"Each reading turns an actual urban location into something other than itself — a forbidden city impersonated, tourism become prison, glamour frozen into province, a metropolis stolen by clandestine filming. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Courtroom as the Spectator's Own Mirror","laconic":"The trial tries the watcher, not the accused.","note":"Each reading turns Saint Omer's tribunal inward: the proceeding becomes a screen onto which Rama projects her dread, her dissolving certainties, her unfinished self. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Comedian Reborn as Serious Auteur","laconic":"Critics startled that genre-comic talent could direct with auteur seriousness.","note":"Each reading registers the same surprise: a figure coded as comic or commercial is suddenly granted directorial gravitas, the praise tinged with condescension about prior expectations. The code is the upgrade-by-astonishment, where craft is validated only against assumed limitation.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Vampire Bound By Moral Law","laconic":"Predators who impose Kantian ethics upon their own appetite.","note":"Both readings cast the vampire not as id unleashed but as a creature governing its bloodlust through self-legislated duty. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Sachi Inherits the Wound She Judges","laconic":"The eldest daughter repeats the parental betrayal she condemns.","note":"Both readings catch Sachi reenacting the very abandonment she resents in her father, the caregiver role folding into the wound she inherits. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Title That Names An Absence","laconic":"Titles that assert presence only to confess its negation.","note":"Each reading treats the film's title as a grammatical act of subtraction—naming a self, a man, or an existence precisely by what is missing, withdrawn, or merely attendant. The title becomes the site where presence is revealed as its own absence.","members":[0,1,2,3,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Prophet Punished For Seeing First","laconic":"The one who saw truth early and was scorned for it.","note":"Each reading frames a figure whose accurate foresight or testimony is met with disbelief, ridicule, or destruction rather than gratitude. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Charge That Indicts Its Accuser","laconic":"A critic's dismissal recast as the critic's own failure of grammar.","note":"Both readings flip a negative critical verdict ('excess', 'self-indulgent pastiche') into a symptom of critical inadequacy rather than authorial fault. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Manic Defense Against Unbearable Knowledge","laconic":"Ritual, beauty, and busyness erected as bulwarks against intolerable loss.","note":"Each reading names a compulsive aesthetic or domestic practice as a psychic shield warding off grief and annihilation. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Villain Who Did the Math","laconic":"Antagonists whose sound utilitarian arithmetic damns the soul behind it.","note":"Each reading frames a figure as a cold consequentialist whose calculus is internally valid yet morally monstrous, and treats the film as the verdict against that calculus. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Liquor As The Film's Operating Logic","laconic":"Drink is not theme but engine — it generates the world.","note":"Each reading treats alcohol not as subject matter but as the substance that powers the film's surreal recurrence, looping time, or claim on the night. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Apple That Decodes the Film","laconic":"A single apple becomes the key unlocking the whole work's meaning.","note":"Each reading elevates the apple from prop to interpretive cipher — the object whose true reading retroactively decrypts perception, falling, or the entire narrative. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Western Shot In Recession's Wreckage","laconic":"American genre filmed amid the 2008 financial ruin it inhabits.","note":"Each reading reframes a road or western film as documentary of post-crash dispossession, shooting in the literal economic wreckage it depicts. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Compression As A Formal Cruelty","laconic":"Temporal squeezing that withholds consolation and forges grief into form.","note":"Each reading treats narrative or temporal compression not as economy but as an aesthetic act of cruelty, where collapsing duration becomes a formal weapon against mourning or relief. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Postcard Landscape Refuted","laconic":"Sun-soaked tourist locales unmasked as exclusion, dispossession, or estrangement.","note":"Each reading takes a famously picturesque destination and reads its glossy surface against itself, exposing the underclass, ownership, or alienation the postcard suppresses. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Pessoa's Trunk Of Multiplied Selves","laconic":"The self splits into unread, overlaid heteronyms.","note":"Both readings invoke Pessoa's fragmented authorship — the self as a trunk of unfinished, multiplied identities. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Camera As Subaltern Survival","laconic":"To photograph the favela is to escape being its corpse.","note":"Both readings cast Rocket's camera as the one tool that lets the slum's narrator outlive and out-author the violence that would otherwise speak for him. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Instrumental Reason As Engine Of Atrocity","laconic":"When rationality optimizes means and forgets the human end.","note":"Each reading indicts instrumental reason — the calculus that reduces persons to means, processes, or targets. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Matchmaking Rite As Economic Conscription","laconic":"Courtship unmasked as a market that drafts and prices bodies.","note":"Each reading exposes the marriage ritual as a hidden economy — auditioning, conscripting, brokering, pricing human beings under romance's cover. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Vanishing Class Hidden In Its Token","laconic":"A privileged order survives only as a defect or absent sign.","note":"Each reading locates a dying social class not in its presence but in a residue—a missing joint, borrowed cultural authority, an absent master. The class is legible only through what it lacks.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Title Names Its Own Thesis","laconic":"The film's title is read as its entire interpretive key.","note":"Each reading treats the title's noun — Neighbor, Weather, Child of Weather — as the whole argument, collapsing the film into its name. The recurring move: the title is not a label but the thesis itself.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Black-And-White As The Solo Auteur's Budget","laconic":"Monochrome read as the signature of one-man, low-cost production.","note":"Both readings treat Hong Sang-soo's grayscale not as aesthetic choice but as the visible economy of a self-sufficient, single-author studio. A genuine recurring interpretive code.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Mathematician Who Starved For His Theorem","laconic":"Genius pursued to the point of bodily self-denial.","note":"A figure whose mathematical or intellectual pursuit becomes ascetic starvation, the mind consuming the body. The drilling of Pi belongs here as the literal flesh-as-solution to an unsolvable proof.","members":[2,3,4]},{"name":"The Mathematician Who Could Not Trust His Mind","laconic":"Clarity as pathology; reason turned against the reasoner.","note":"The thinker whose lucidity is reframed as madness, unable to distinguish his own logic from delusion. Cobb's collapsing dreamscape and Wheeler's pathologized sanity share this code of reason indicting itself."}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Held Breath Beneath The Surface","laconic":"Submersion and suspended breath as rehearsals of loss.","note":"Each reading frames diving, drowning, or breath-holding as a held suspension between life and death — the underwater as a space of arrested grief or unresurfaced fate.","members":[0,1,2,3,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Body Sold As Property","laconic":"Persons rendered as merchandise — the trafficked figure as commodity.","note":"Each reading turns a vulnerable body — child, daughter, spirit, gynoid — into a unit of exchange, indicting the marketplace that prices personhood. The cluster coheres around trafficking-as-commodification.","members":[0,1,2,4,5]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Loyal Blade That Cannot Disobey","laconic":"The retainer whose honor is his cage of obedience.","note":"A recurring code: the warrior bound to a master or power, his loyalty an unbreakable, often fatal command. The film stages devotion to authority as a form of doom.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Choreography Before Psychology","laconic":"Bodies in motion, not interiority, generate meaning and dread.","note":"Each reading insists the film's truth is staged through movement and blocking rather than performed feeling or character interiority. The Dardennes' kinetic pursuit, Possession's danced horror, and Wild Goose Lake's velocity all locate meaning in the choreographed body first.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Tanizaki's Shadows Against The Neon City","laconic":"Tokyo read through Tanizaki's elegy of vanishing shadow.","note":"These readings invoke Tanizaki's 'In Praise of Shadows' as a lens on a luminous, alienating Tokyo where old darkness loses to neon. Both films are framed as battlegrounds between shadow and glare.","members":[0,3]},{"name":"The Blue Hour Where Forgiveness Fails","laconic":"Tokyo Twilight as the darkening dusk of mercy.","note":"Both readings pin on the title's twilight ('boshoku') as the moment forgiveness curdles, positioning the film as Shochiku's somber rejoinder to the Taiyozoku.","members":[1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Drum Sequence As Embedded Cipher","laconic":"A drum performance encodes the entire film in miniature.","note":"Both readings treat a drum-driven spectacle not as set piece but as the film's interpretive key—a sequence that contains, or exposes, the whole.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Eternal Forest Is A Working Landscape","laconic":"Mythic, timeless woods are actually managed, vanishing, or fabricated terrain.","note":"Each reading punctures the diegetic illusion of a primeval, eternal grove by naming the real, worked, or constructed ground beneath it. The sacred forest is exposed as plantation, plateau, or pond.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Wilmington Stands In For Everywhere","laconic":"A real production town doubles as fictional anyplace.","note":"Both readings expose Wilmington, North Carolina as the material substrate beneath glossy fictional geographies, where the actual site of manufacture leaks through the diegetic location it impersonates.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Woman Who Vanishes As Structuring Absence","laconic":"A woman's disappearance becomes the text's organizing void.","note":"Each reading treats a vanished woman not as plot but as the absent center that structures the entire work — the vanishing point around which meaning organizes. The disappearance is the form, not the event.","members":[0,1,2,3,4,5]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Director Who Owns His Cast","laconic":"Filmmaker as cult-master, possessing performers body and will.","note":"Both readings cast Murata as a director whose authority becomes total ownership—Pygmalion sculptor and carceral institution fused into one figure of consuming control.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Summer Acquitted, The Lover Indicted","laconic":"Readings that flip blame onto Tom's projection, exonerating Summer.","note":"Each line dismantles the romantic-victim framing, exposing Tom's love as self-serving fantasy and Summer as the film's honest party. The audience's hatred of Summer becomes evidence of the misreading the film diagnoses.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Setting Clocks To A Distant Beloved","laconic":"Time-adjustment as a magical act of longing across distance.","note":"All three read the film's clock-resetting as sympathetic magic — bending time to bridge separation, whether the dead, the absent traveler, or a foreign metropole. The code is the manipulated clock as an instrument of love and longing.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Flower That Indicts the Forgetful Reader","laconic":"A blossom encodes a truth the man cannot read.","note":"Each reading treats a flower (rose, cactus rose) as a legible sign of unacknowledged love or repressed history that the male recipient fails or refuses to decode. The florist and the unknown woman alike address a reader who cannot read the message.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"Desire That Feeds On Its Own Frustration","laconic":"Appetite sustained, not satisfied, by the obstacle it meets.","note":"Both films stage longing as a self-administering system that requires deferral and obstruction to keep itself alive. Desire becomes a managed economy rather than a drive toward consummation.","members":[0,4]},{"name":"Living Postponed Into Bureaucratic Deferral","laconic":"Life held in abeyance by procedure and delay.","note":"The film treats vitality itself as something endlessly deferred through administrative routine, action perpetually postponed.","members":[1]},{"name":"The Self Dissolved Into Pleasureless Performance","laconic":"Identity worn as costume over an absent, joyless core.","note":"Both readings locate a hollowed interior — performance standing in for selfhood, anhedonia as the residue beneath the act.","members":[3,5]},{"name":"The Disenchantment Of The World","laconic":"Magic stripped from the field by cold calculation.","note":"A Weberian reading of statistical rationalization displacing romance and myth.","members":[2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Snow That Erases The World","laconic":"Whiteout as void, erasure, the map blanked into memory.","note":"These readings all treat snow not as weather but as a force of erasure — voiding map, memory, witness, or national self into white. The recurring move converts real winter into a semiotic blanking.","members":[1,3,4,5,6,7]},{"name":"The Real Snow That Refuses Metaphor","laconic":"Actual snowfall resists the script's designs and meaning-making.","note":"A distinct counter-code: snow here stays stubbornly material, forcing tragedy or defying figuration rather than dissolving into symbol.","members":[0,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Plot That Was Never Hers","laconic":"A woman framed as subject is really the deceptive surface of male delusion.","note":"All three readings circle the same code: the woman appears central but is a screen onto which paranoid male vision projects. Even the critics inherit the protagonist's misreading—the device folds the audience into the delusion.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Coney Island As America's Last Stop","laconic":"The boardwalk edge where the national promise dead-ends into ocean.","note":"Both readings cast Coney Island as a terminal frontier — the point where the city's or nation's promise exhausts itself against the shore. The shared device of the edge-of-map periphery makes this one code.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Witness Who Records His Own Erasure","laconic":"Bearing testimony while one's own body and memory dissolve.","note":"The diarist-witness whose act of recording is inseparable from documenting his own dying — testimony as a race against personal oblivion. [2] is the bomb's maker repenting, a different code entirely, and stands alone.","members":[0,1,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Praise That Confesses the Critic's Appetite","laconic":"Aesthetic acclaim exposes the reviewer's own gaze and need.","note":"Each reading turns critical praise back on the critic, treating words like 'sensuous,' 'empathy,' or 'hypnotic' as confessions of the reviewer's hunger to look or be reassured. The code is reception-as-self-incrimination.","members":[0,1,2,5]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The War Wound That Cannot Be Absolved","laconic":"The surviving soldier as pilgrim through inexpiable guilt.","note":"The veteran does not heal but carries a haunting that demands penance no confession can grant. Survival itself becomes the unpayable debt.","members":[0,3]},{"name":"The Battlefield Rendered As Expressionist Canvas","laconic":"War and city composed as painted, trembling distortion.","note":"The frame abandons documentary realism for the warped lines of Expressionist art — the world bent into a graphic, hand-drawn nightmare.","members":[1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Pleasure Principle Versus The Reality Principle","laconic":"Comedies as battlegrounds of Freudian wish and consequence.","note":"Each reading stages the film as a contest between unbound wish-fulfillment and the sobering intrusion of reality, whether the wish wins or is defeated. [2] is a slightly different angle on Home Alone's wish but stays within the same psychoanalytic code.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Blockbuster Engineered For Its Cultural Moment","laconic":"Spectacle calibrated to box-office math and the era's politics.","note":"Both readings treat the tentpole film as a product reverse-engineered from market timing and the surrounding cultural conversation. The text becomes an artifact of demographic and political calculation rather than authorship.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Bourgeoisie Imprisoned In Itself","laconic":"Class position becomes the inescapable room, family, or trap.","note":"Each reading locates bourgeois identity as a self-enclosing structure — flat, family, salon — that cannot be exited or renounced. The punishment is reproduction of the same.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Heavenly Tribunal As Postwar Geopolitics","laconic":"The celestial court arbitrates which empire and alliance survives the peace.","note":"Both readings recast Powell-Pressburger's afterlife trial as a verdict on postwar power: the Marshall Plan and the survival of empire litigated as cosmic law. The court is geopolitics in robes.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Dignity As Borrowed Costume, Not Birthright","laconic":"Dignity worn as external prop rather than possessed as inner right.","note":"Each reading treats dignity as something staged, donned, or stripped from outside — a uniform, a posted line, a costume mistaken for virtue — rather than an inalienable inner endowment. The Nickel Boys entry tests precisely that Kantian inner dignity to destruction, sharpening the cluster's shared wound.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Name Inherited Versus The Name Chosen","laconic":"Lineage as destiny wars with the self-elected identity.","note":"These readings all turn on whether a name—Skywalker, Jedi, Rogue—is bloodline given or willfully claimed. The cluster stages a single quarrel between inheritance and self-authorship.","members":[1,4,5,6]},{"name":"The Sword That Smuggles A Politics","laconic":"The elegant blade encodes a reactionary, weather-like order.","note":"Two readings treat the lightsaber/war not as plot but as ideology: the 'civilized' weapon carrying reactionary politics, and war as permanent cosmic weather.","members":[2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Poet Hidden in the Working Man","laconic":"Art made quietly by one whose day job conceals it.","note":"Each reading insists the true poet wears the uniform of ordinary labor—bus driver, executive, laborer—creating in stolen hours unseen by the world. The device locates greatness inside anonymous routine.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The West Anoints India As Its Antidote","laconic":"Western acclaim rewards Indian films for not being 'Indian' enough.","note":"Each reading exposes how Western reception (Cannes, critics) prizes Indian cinema precisely when it flatters the West's appetite for a quiet, un-Bollywood India. The praise becomes a mirror of the praiser's own craving rather than the film's substance.","members":[0,1,2,3,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Institution Unmasked As Theater","laconic":"Wards, locker rooms, homes revealed as compulsory stages.","note":"Each reading exposes an institution — asylum, jock house, recovering home — as a performance where inmates are costumed players forced to enact sanity, masculinity, or wellness before a watching tribunal. The 'Follies' that name themselves a comedy crown the figure.","members":[1,2,3,4,5]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Atrocity Survived Only By Reenacting It","laconic":"Killers and victims metabolize violence by staging it as performance.","note":"Both readings turn on the same code: horror becomes bearable, even reproducible, only when re-performed as theater. The pun on 'act' (deed/performance) is the shared semiotic hinge.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Cosmos Wired By Coincidence, Not Cause","laconic":"Events rhyme by synchronicity; causation is quietly dethroned.","note":"Both readings claim the film's secret physics is meaningful coincidence rather than chains of cause and effect. The plot's connective tissue is cosmic rhyme, not motivation.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"Duty As The Maxim Made Universal","laconic":"The act tested against whether its maxim could be willed for all.","note":"These readings explicitly stage the categorical imperative — self-legislation, universalizable disclosure, conscience-as-duty — as the engine or the horror of the act. Each frames a deed as Kantian law enacted.","members":[0,1,2,4,6]},{"name":"The Verdict The Enforcer Will Not Own","laconic":"He carries out the judgment he refuses to author.","note":"A distinct code: the agent of punishment disclaims the sentence he enforces, splitting deed from authorship. The hunter and the bookkeeping husband mistake mechanism for justice.","members":[5,7]},{"name":"He Sentences Himself Before The World Can","laconic":"Guilt is self-administered, preempting any external tribunal.","note":"Conscience here forecloses on itself — the boy punishes himself, the foreclosed conscience finds its calm. Self-condemnation arrives ahead of judgment.","members":[8,11]},{"name":"No Freedom, No Guilt, No Goodness","laconic":"Moral status requires the capacity that the situation denies.","note":"These pose the formal precondition of morality: a man who cannot sin isn't good, guilt without freedom is incoherent. The argument is about whether the agent could be moral at all.","members":[9,10]},{"name":"Sleep As The Privilege Of The Guilty","laconic":"The guilty rest; the conscience-bound cannot.","note":"This inverts the expected — restless guilt — into the guilty sleeping well. It stands alone, sharing only ambient moral vocabulary with the cluster.","members":[3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Frame That Confesses Its Own Fiction","laconic":"A film's outer device admits the whole image was staged.","note":"These readings each locate meaning in a framing device — documentary conceit, theatrical bow, narration, crooked sets — that turns on itself to confess its own artifice. The frame stops being neutral and becomes the film's theory of its own image.","members":[0,1,5,6,7,8]},{"name":"The Specimen In Suspended Judgment","laconic":"A caged figure becomes the film's own withheld verdict.","note":"Both stage a confined exhibit — genius in prison, geek in formaldehyde — read as the work's self-suspended sentence on itself.","members":[2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Goya's Black Paintings As Filming Manual","laconic":"Each film read through Goya's pitiless late-period dark canvases.","note":"Both readings recruit Goya's Black Paintings as the interpretive key — a single recurring code where the painter's bleak, deformed grotesque becomes the lens for monochrome cruelty. The convergence is exact: not 'art-influenced cinema' but specifically these darkest works.","members":[0,1]}]}
