{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Well As The Threshold Of Recognition","laconic":"Water demanded or denied marks the law of the stranger.","note":"In each, a site of water (drowning face, murder at the well, demand for drink) becomes the scene where the stranger is either admitted into the human order or refused it. Thirst and its answer adjudicate who counts as a person.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Rescue She Locks Out","laconic":"The drowning chosen over the hand offered.","note":"Both Casino Royale readings converge on Vesper's self-sealing—the shower collapse as the repressed kill resurfacing, the locked door as refused rescue. One code: the woman who guards her death from intervention.","members":[1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Burma That Japan Filmed To Avoid Itself","laconic":"Burmese setting as displaced screen for Japan's unfaced war guilt.","note":"Both readings treat the film's Burma as a fabricated elsewhere — pagodas that were never Burma — onto which postwar Japan projects what it cannot confront directly.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Conqueror Devoured By His Own Empire","laconic":"Imperial obsessives outlived and consumed by the conquest that defined them.","note":"Each names a colonial or frontier figure whose drive to conquer becomes a self-consuming destiny — the empire-builder stalked, doomed, or outlived by his own project. Index [3] reads as a vanity-and-validation note rather than imperial self-destruction, and stands apart.","members":[0,1,2,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Land That Outlasts God's Name","laconic":"Iceland resists the priest's faith and the empire's tongue alike.","note":"Both readings frame the Icelandic terrain as a force that refuses the colonizer's meaning—indifferent to the missionary's God and to the two imperial names imposed upon it. The land is the silent victor over imported significance.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Glass Cathedral Of Colonial Hong Kong","laconic":"Shattering glass reads as the breaking colonial mirror.","note":"Both readings cast the Wing On store's glass as a colonial edifice whose destruction stages Hong Kong's pre-1997 reckoning. The shattering becomes a semiotic event, not mere spectacle.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Earthquake That Authored Its Own Cinema","laconic":"Catastrophe and erasable terrain become the very ground of Kiarostami's filmmaking.","note":"Each reading treats the Manjil-Rudbar quake and the fragile Koker geography not as backdrop but as the generative force and threatened subject of the films themselves. The land's vulnerability is read as the origin and stake of the cinema.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"What Lies Beneath The Surface Speaks","laconic":"Truth is submerged; the real self lives underwater.","note":"Each reading locates the authentic self or meaning below the surface — drowned, sunken, silent — requiring descent to recover it. The watery depth is the code of buried truth.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Crime Retold Until Truth Dissolves","laconic":"Nested testimonies contradict until no single account survives.","note":"Each reading invokes the Rashomon/bamboo-grove structure: an event recounted through competing, irreconcilable testimonies that destabilize the very notion of fact. The frame story becomes a tribunal where judgment reverses and truth refuses to settle.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Her Silence Is The Argument, Not The Absence","laconic":"Female silence reread as authored stance, not lack or wound.","note":"Each reading inverts the default: her not-speaking is recast as agency, knowledge, refusal, or the film's true subject—silence as authored position rather than mystery or trauma to be solved. The set coheres tightly around silence reclaimed as meaning.","members":[0,1,2,4,5,6,7,8]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Train As Nation In Transit","laconic":"The rail carriage stages the modern nation's history and breakdown.","note":"Each reading treats the train not as setting but as compressed allegory for the nation-state—its modernization, its liberal order, its destination it cannot reach. The carriage becomes a moving microcosm of the polity.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Real Thief Wears A Vault","laconic":"The bank, not the robber, is the true heist.","note":"Both readings invert the crime: foreclosure is the original robbery, and the men loot the institution that looted them. The code reframes legitimate finance as the genuine theft.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Refusal To Become One's Assigned Self","laconic":"Declining the polished, promoted, predestined identity as authentic act.","note":"Across these readings the gesture is identical: a subject refuses the self handed to them — stardom, promotion, category, predestination — and that very negation becomes the authentic act. The recurring 'refusal as authenticity' move is the loaded code.","members":[0,2,3,4,5,7]},{"name":"Refusal As The World's Stubborn Facticity","laconic":"Saying no makes reality, body, and tradition assert themselves.","note":"Here refusal is not self-fashioning but resistance against an imposed order — the blade, the seat, the world's brute insistence. The 'no' confronts external power rather than constructing an inner self.","members":[1,6]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Clumsy Zoom As Visible Improvisation","laconic":"Hong's imprecise zoom betrays the hand writing scenes that morning.","note":"Every reading treats the rough, manual zoom as the legible trace of same-day, improvised authorship — the camera's clumsiness as the signature of a cinema written at dawn. Even the 'poverty aesthetic' entry folds in as the same gesture reframed as economic necessity turned style.","members":[0,1,2,3,4,5]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Cranes Fly On, Indifferent To Grief","laconic":"Nature's migration overrides human mourning; the title names cosmic indifference.","note":"Both readings invert the lyrical title into a verdict on nature's refusal to grieve. The cranes' flight becomes proof that the world continues, unmoved by the lovers' loss.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Mission Names Its Own Impossibility","laconic":"The franchise title indexes the contradiction at the heart of each plot.","note":"Both readings treat the word 'Impossible' as a self-referential code rather than mere genre branding — one finds it in the self-negating order, the other relocates it from spy-work to marriage. Together they form a recurring move: read the title as a thesis about what cannot be reconciled.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Convent As Forced-Birth Apparatus","laconic":"Post-Dobbs nun-horror reads divine pregnancy as compulsory pregnancy.","note":"Each reading converts the sacred-conception convent into an allegory of bodily autonomy stripped away, the womb as contested property after Dobbs. The recurrence of nuns, conspiracy, and unwilled gestation makes this a genuine activated code, not a mere theme.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Clerk Who Dreamed Past The Ledger","laconic":"The cubicle drone whose inner life overflows the balance sheet.","note":"A recurring figure: the bookkeeper, accountant, or clerk whose ledger-bound existence is the very thing the film wants to escape, transcend, or expose as a void. The code activates the expectation that the numbers conceal a longing—or an emptiness—the columns cannot tally.","members":[0,1,2,3,4,5,6]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Landscape Filmed As Its Own Drowning","laconic":"Chinese terrain shot as a place already submerged, eulogizing a vanishing nation.","note":"Each reading treats the physical setting—riverbank, gorge, mining town, condemned city—as a body of water or grave closing over a civilization, turning geography into elegy. The drowned-Tang/Du Fu and demolition readings share one code: the land filmed at the waterline of its own erasure.","members":[0,1,2,3,4,5]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Body That Is Secretly A Machine","laconic":"Flesh and feeling reframed as mechanism, engine, or corrosive apparatus.","note":"Each reading dissolves the boundary between organism and machinery — the ship-as-body, the flesh-machine, love rendered as engine or contagion. The shared move is treating human intimacy and embodiment as a mechanical system.","members":[0,2,3]},{"name":"Romance As Networked Financial Contagion","laconic":"Affection read as the smiling face of systemic economic collapse.","note":"This reading is doing something distinct: it maps a digital love-figure onto the 2008 financial crisis as contagion, a socioeconomic allegory rather than a body-machine fusion.","members":[1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Refusal of Forgiveness as Sovereignty","laconic":"Withholding pardon becomes the wronged self's final claim to power.","note":"Each reading reframes refusing forgiveness not as bitterness but as a sovereign, justice-bearing act — the victim seizing moral authority by denying absolution. The recurrence of the exact phrase 'refusal of forgiveness' across all three makes this a tight, genuine code.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Lie That Performs Itself Into Truth","laconic":"Feigned blindness as fiction that overtakes and becomes its own reality.","note":"Both readings of Andhadhun treat the performed deception not as ruse but as ontological engine—the lie does not conceal truth, it manufactures it. The spectator's faith in confession or conscience is itself exposed as the deepest fiction.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Scored Against The Copland American Pastoral","laconic":"Music summoned and inverted to interrogate the mythic American landscape.","note":"Both readings position their soundtracks in dialogue with Copland's open-prairie Americana — one inverting it, one setting fiddle against it. The shared interpretive move is reading score as argument with a national pastoral idiom.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Scar's Reign As Honest Governance","laconic":"The usurper exposes the kingdom's hidden political truths.","note":"Both readings rehabilitate Scar as the regime that speaks the real logic of power and scarcity, treating the 'rightful' order as the actual fiction. The trope inverts villain and statesman.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Director Who Refuses Sovereign Detachment","laconic":"The watcher who will not stay safely outside the frame.","note":"These readings cast the observing intelligence — director, spectator, experimenter — as ethically compromised by the very act of watching, unable to remain a neutral outsider. The refusal or impossibility of detached witnessing is the shared code.","members":[0,1,2]},{"name":"The Observer Who Speaks Through Composition","laconic":"Silence and framing become the witness's only true speech.","note":"Here the watching figure renounces words and indicts or testifies purely through mute arrangement — the silent servants, the wordless observer composing meaning by image alone.","members":[3,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Title That Names Its Effect","laconic":"The film's name announces its function, not its tale.","note":"These readings treat the title as a performative label — a word denoting effect or affect rather than naming a character or plot. [1] and [2] explicitly read 'Terrifier' as a function-name; [0] reads 'Shrek' as terror-word turned love-name.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Symmetry As The Architecture Of Power","laconic":"Compositional balance read not as beauty but as coercion's visible form.","note":"Each reading inverts the classical equation of symmetry with harmony, recasting the balanced frame as an instrument of repression, hierarchy, and tyranny. The shared move is precise: order in composition exposes order imposed by power.","members":[0,2,3,4]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Woman Who Keeps A Dead Code","laconic":"She inherits jianghu loyalty after the order has been liquidated.","note":"Qiao becomes the lone faithful custodian of an honor-code that capital and time have already killed. The reading recurs as woman-as-widow of a vanished moral order.","members":[5,6,7,8]},{"name":"The Bride Sold Into Her Own Authorship","laconic":"A transacted woman converts captivity into a self she writes against fate.","note":"Both readings turn a woman's sale/confinement within a gilded patriarchal household into the ground from which she authors selfhood. The transaction is the prison and the paradoxical origin of agency.","members":[2,4]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"There Is No Self Beneath The Role","laconic":"Identity as performance with no authentic core underneath.","note":"Both readings dissolve the self into a recursion of roles, denying any stable interiority beneath the theatrical mask.","members":[1,4]},{"name":"Eve As Predatory Engine Of Substitution","laconic":"The understudy who wants not the part but the person.","note":"These cast Eve as a consuming logic—capital, mimetic desire—that seeks not Margo's role but to replace Margo herself.","members":[2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Beautiful Machine That Demands Immolation","laconic":"Speed and the machine aestheticized until they detonate their worshipper.","note":"Each reading treats velocity or the engine as a Futurist object of worship whose logic culminates in the gorgeous crash or self-detonation. The machine is loved precisely as it consumes its rider.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Badge As Tested Conscience","laconic":"The lawman whose integrity is the true plot.","note":"These readings cast the officer not as crimefighter but as a vessel of conscience under pressure — refusing the bribe, throwing down the badge, bleeding for it, burning out. The badge is a moral test, and the film's drama is whether the man keeps faith with it.","members":[0,2,5,6,7]},{"name":"The Law's Indistinguishable Double","laconic":"The cop who is the state's interchangeable or compromised instrument.","note":"Here the officer is read as substitutable or secretly the system's asset — authority performed as facade, identity collapsed into the apparatus rather than tested against it.","members":[1,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Stillness As Stateless Sovereignty","laconic":"Elia Suleiman's frozen body politicizes immobility into deadpan resistance.","note":"Both readings locate Suleiman's signature device: the motionless, mute observer whose very stillness becomes a political and comedic act. The shared code is immobility weaponized — stillness as the dispossessed subject's only available form of agency.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Ending That Confesses Its Own Impossibility","laconic":"Closure withheld as the truest admission a film can make.","note":"Each reading treats the film's ending as a confession — that it cannot, will not, or must not be authored. The act of not-ending becomes the work's deepest gesture toward truth.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Title That Names Eden's Forbidden Fruit","laconic":"Titles invoke the Genesis pact: knowledge bought at paradise's price.","note":"Each reading reads its title as a scriptural cipher — Eden, the Fall, the lethal cost of knowing. The films are recast as variations on the expulsion from the garden.","members":[0,1,2,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Secret Whose Function Outlives Its Content","laconic":"What's carried matters; what it contains is beside the point.","note":"These readings treat the secret/password/code as a structural engine—its narrative work lies in transmission, concealment, or repression, never in its actual disclosure. The content is a MacGuffin; the carrying is the meaning.","members":[0,2,3,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The City Conjured On A Hollywood Stage","laconic":"Iconic metropolises rebuilt as soundstage illusions in California.","note":"Each reading exposes a famous city — New York, Neverland-as-elsewhere — fabricated on Culver City or Sony soundstages. The trope activates the expectation that the place we 'see' is a backlot disguise.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"Murder Redeemed As Aesthetic, Not Moral, Act","laconic":"Killing reframed as a category of beauty, beyond ethics.","note":"These readings strip murder of moral weight and recast it as an aesthetic gesture — beauty, style, or pure form supplanting good and evil.","members":[0,1,3,5,9,10]},{"name":"The Gentle Killer Without Cruelty","laconic":"Violence rendered tender, serene, drained of malice and despair.","note":"A distinct code where the act of killing is marked by gentleness and calm rather than aestheticized transgression — the assassin who kills softly.","members":[2,7]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Son Who Becomes The Devouring Father","laconic":"Filial inheritance as patricide and self-annihilation.","note":"Both readings trace how the heir is consumed by — and becomes — the paternal order, piety curdling into self-erasure.","members":[0,1]},{"name":"The Disavowed Self Returning To Be Killed","laconic":"The repressed comes back externalized, then must die.","note":"Each reading locates a buried self or unwanted truth projected outward — as a person, a child, or a fist — only to be violently confronted or eliminated. The return of the repressed made flesh.","members":[2,3,4,5,6]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Title That Names The Hunter, Not The Hunt","laconic":"Predation as the world's weather; the prey carries the gun.","note":"These readings reframe the hunt-title to expose who is truly predator and prey — the aftermath as the real predation, the prey who carries the gun, predation as permanent weather, the stalker forbidden the kill.","members":[0,6,8,9]},{"name":"The Hunt-Word That Hides A Different Meaning","laconic":"'Hunt' decoded as goodwill, no quarry, a chorus, a trap.","note":"Each reading detonates a pun or false expectation buried in the title — goodwill instead of a manhunt, a hunt with no quarry, a chorus instead of a beast, an assault that names its own trap.","members":[1,3,5,10]},{"name":"The 'After' That Reveals No After Exists","laconic":"The aftermath dissolves into the absence of any after.","note":"Titles built on 'after' are read as collapsing temporality: time as the aftermath of attention, the discovery that there is no after.","members":[2,7]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Seasons That Decode The Film","laconic":"Seasonal naming as the secret key to a film's structure.","note":"Each reading treats a seasonal sign—a name, a reversal, a calendar—as the cipher that unlocks the whole narrative. The season isn't atmosphere; it's the encoded meaning the film hands you.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Tape That Records But Never Replays","laconic":"Compulsive filming substitutes for living; the footage stays forever unwatched.","note":"Each reading fixates on the camcorder as a device that captures experience in place of having it, hoarding tapes no one will ever screen. The mother-wound variant deepens the same code into the psychology of compulsive recording.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Real Town Repainted Into A Dream","laconic":"An actual working city repainted until reality becomes an unsustainable stage-set.","note":"Both readings catch Demy's signature gesture: the documentary location colonized by candy color until the real place is transfigured into a fragile musical dream. The 'repainting' is the code — artifice imposed on the actual, a dream that cannot hold.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Lost Decade Reading Itself As Drifting Youth","laconic":"Japan's recession refracted through precarious workers and stalled lives.","note":"Each reading maps a film onto Japan's post-bubble economic malaise—the freeter, the unemployed son, the labor market—turning private drama into socioeconomic allegory. The shared move is the insistence on the Lost Decade as the hidden subject.","members":[0,1,3,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Real Author History Credited To Another","laconic":"The true agent erased; the legend keeps the name.","note":"Each reading insists the actual doer—the indispensable man, the cracker, the engine, the discoverer—is written out while another inherits the credit. The trope is authorship stolen by the official record.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Watching Our Species Go Extinct","laconic":"Naturalist observation turned on humanity's own quiet vanishing.","note":"Both readings treat the film as a documentary gaze pointed inward, framing human behavior as a species nearing extinction. The misheard Attenborough name encodes the same wildlife-observation conceit.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Theft As Claim Against Property's Law","laconic":"Taking reframed as right, resistance, or survival — never mere crime.","note":"These readings recast theft as a moral or political counter-claim against the regime of property: gleaning, shoplifting, identity theft, borrowing become assertions of a prior or denied right. The shared move is the inversion that locates justice in the taker, not the law.","members":[2,4,7,11]},{"name":"Theft As The Logic Of Capital Itself","laconic":"Stealing as the system's own compulsion, not its violation.","note":"Here theft is not opposed to capital but its hidden grammar — extraction, repetition compulsion, the firm, the laundering of transgression into genius. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Eastern Margin As Europe's Repressed Body","laconic":"Romanian/Eastern labor and bodies as the EU's disavowed unconscious.","note":"Each reading stages a peripheral European space — workers, cities, subtitles — as the return of what a 'reunified' Europe represses about its own labor, migration, and Babel-like fractures. The cluster coheres as one interpretive move: the East as continental guilty conscience.","members":[0,1,2,3,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"O'Keeffe's Bleached West As Sacred Emptiness","laconic":"The desert framed through O'Keeffe's painterly mythology of bones and void.","note":"Both readings invoke O'Keeffe to sanctify an emptied Western landscape, reading the desert as a painterly icon of purity and absence. The shared device is the explicit O'Keeffe analogy, not merely 'the West.'","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Mountain Kingdom Lost To Exile","laconic":"Erebor as homeland of a stateless, wandering people.","note":"Both readings cast Erebor not as treasure-hoard but as the lost nation that defines a displaced people's identity. The mountain is a homeland, the dwarves a diaspora.","members":[3,4]},{"name":"The Reluctant Crown And Its Sickness","laconic":"The would-be king poisoned by the very restoration he seeks.","note":"Kingship here is a malady, not a triumph — the heir sickens on his own restoration, or shoulders command he never wanted. Power read as affliction rather than reward.","members":[1,5]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Witness Whose Testimony Is Silence","laconic":"Those who see the crime but cannot, or will not, speak it.","note":"Each centers a witness whose muteness — chosen, imposed, or born of trauma — becomes the only available form of testimony. The silence is not absence but an act, a drawing, a photograph standing in for the unspeakable.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Cave Painters Beneath The Village","laconic":"Lascaux's prehistoric violence haunting a tidy modern town.","note":"Both readings root Chabrol's killer in deep time, reading the nearby cave paintings as the buried, unbroken lineage of human butchery beneath provincial calm.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Final Boy As Slapstick Martyr","laconic":"Survival rendered as involuntary physical comedy performed under torment.","note":"Both readings recast the horror survivor as a body conscripted into performance — Keaton-esque pratfall, accidental showmanship — making endurance itself a slapstick act. The cluster coheres on the protagonist-as-comic-victim code shared across the Evil Dead pair.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Confession Addressed To No One Present","laconic":"Speech aimed past the listener, toward an absent Other.","note":"Each reading hears intimate address that bypasses its ostensible recipient, speaking instead to a structural void or invisible audience. {"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Captain Who Needs A Remembered Foe","laconic":"Hook's villainy depends on Peter recalling who he was.","note":"These readings treat Hook's antagonism as relational and ethical — seduction, presence, and the demand for a worthy adversary — all rooted in memory.","members":[1,2]},{"name":"The Hook As The Barb Of The Past","laconic":"The hook names how history sinks into the present.","note":"Both readings hear 'hook' as a wounding instrument of temporal return — the past lodged barbed in the now.","members":[3]},{"name":"The Hook As Barbed Object Of Desire","laconic":"The hook is lack made into curved flesh.","note":"A psychoanalytic and material-historical reading of the literal hook as a charged signifier — Lacanian objet a, the cotton gin's afterlife.","members":[4,5]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Panic Over The Film Confirms The Film","laconic":"The reception's alarm enacts the very thesis on screen.","note":"Each reading argues that the moral panic surrounding a film's release became proof of its argument — the audience's fear completing the work's prophecy. A genuine recurring interpretive move about reception folding back into meaning.","members":[0,1,4]},{"name":"Manufactured Panic As Instrument Of Power","laconic":"Within the film, panic is engineered to rule.","note":"These read panic as a depicted device of control inside the narrative, not as external reception confirming the work. A distinct code about fear as political instrument.","members":[2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"Love As Espionage Continued By Other Means","laconic":"Intimacy becomes the covert operation it pretends to escape.","note":"Romance is figured as tradecraft — affection indistinguishable from surveillance, recruitment, or the agent's return. The lovers cannot stop spying even when they love.","members":[1,5]},{"name":"The State That Pimps Its Patriots As Duty","laconic":"Patriotism rebranded as the sanctioned prostitution of the loyal.","note":"A reading that exposes how institutions weaponize devotion, selling intimacy and the body under the cover of national service. Stands distinct from love-as-espionage in its accusatory political charge.","members":[2]},{"name":"The Felony As The Only Grammar Of Love","laconic":"Tenderness can only be spoken through transgressive acts.","note":"Affection has no licit vocabulary, so it borrows the syntax of crime or interdicted feeling — burglary, jealousy — as its sole available expression. Desire smuggled through the forbidden.","members":[0,3]},{"name":"The Avenger Who Wears Her Target's Soul","laconic":"Vengeance achieved by becoming the thing destroyed.","note":"A singular figure who internalizes the enemy to annihilate it from within. Too specific in its mimetic-revenge logic to merge with the love or espionage codes.","members":[4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Crowd-Pleaser the Avant-Garde Disowned","laconic":"Popular success read as betrayal of cinephilia's cult of rupture.","note":"These readings share a single code: a film's warmth or triumph counted against it by a criticism that prizes radical breakage over pleasure. The misreading reframes accessibility itself as the wound.","members":[1,3,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Figure of Speech Taken Literally","laconic":"A dead idiom revives and enacts its buried meaning.","note":"Each reading turns a worn-out endearment or phrase into literal narrative event — the metaphor cashed in for its hidden cost. The titles themselves are the dormant clichés the films force awake.","members":[1,2]}]}
{"verdict":"reject","groups":[]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Withheld Image That Indicts Us","laconic":"What the frame refuses to show becomes its truth.","note":"Both films pivot on a deliberately unseen image—the capped lens, the absent photograph—whose absence carries the moral and mortal weight. The documentary gaze convicts itself by what it cannot or will not record.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Brand Name As True Protagonist","laconic":"The film's real star is the product it sells.","note":"Both readings displace the human hero, locating the film's identity in a commercial brand that precedes and outlives the story. The brand is the actual character.","members":[2,3]},{"name":"The Fake Footage More Real Than The Film","laconic":"The advertisement or pre-show outshines the feature itself.","note":"These readings claim the embedded fiction-within-fiction — the fake commercial, the four minutes before — is the authentic cinema, demoting the official movie to a frame.","members":[1,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Black-And-White As An Argument, Not A Style","laconic":"Monochrome reframed as a polemic against color's plenitude and present.","note":"Each reading treats the absence of color not as period aesthetic but as a deliberate thesis — refusing the present, indicting digital abundance, or mourning a time that never was. Even They Live fits: grayscale as the revealed truth beneath ideology's color.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Prison Sentence Bought And Sold","laconic":"A jail term becomes property, exposing who owns whose body.","note":"These three readings all turn on the transaction of incarceration in Three Monkeys — a sentence purchased from a poor man, laying bare patronage and bodily ownership. They are facets of one code.","members":[1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The City As Confected Wound Of Longing","laconic":"Paris built from postcard-fantasy to seal an unhealable ache.","note":"Each reading treats the cinematic city not as place but as curated artifice — a theme park or postcard collage — assembled to repress or soothe a longing it can never cure. The constructed setting is itself the symptom.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Withheld Score Is A Moral Refusal","laconic":"Absent music denies catharsis, sentiment, grace—scoring as ethical abstention.","note":"Each reads the missing or restrained score as a deliberate refusal: of comfort, of feeling, of redemption. The silence carries the meaning.","members":[0,1,2,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Universal Backlot Wearing A New Face","laconic":"The same studio backlot redressed to pass for elsewhere.","note":"Each reading exposes Universal's standing sets as a recurring substrate that masquerades as American place. The code is the backlot caught performing locations it can never truly be.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The One Denied The Right To Mourn","laconic":"Grief itself becomes a contested civic entitlement, withheld at the threshold.","note":"Each reading frames mourning not as private feeling but as a public right gatekept by power, gender, or austerity. The recurring move is to expose who is barred from grieving, making the funeral a political frontier.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Camera Interrogates Its Own Witnessing","laconic":"Documentaries whose true subject is the act of bearing witness.","note":"Both readings turn the documentary inward, making the possibility (or impossibility) of witness the actual subject. One affirms witness exists, the other doubts it can — opposite poles of a single self-reflexive code.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Stillness Engineered By Subtraction","laconic":"Performance built by taking away, not adding restraint.","note":"These readings share one device: a flatness, silence, or stillness achieved through removal — the actor or director subtracts rather than performs. The blankness is engineered, the void itself doing the dramaturgical work.","members":[1,3,4,7,8,9,10]},{"name":"Silence That Forces The Eye To Act","laconic":"Withheld voice or sound throws meaning onto the gaze.","note":"Here subtraction is aimed outward: by withholding speech the film conscripts the spectator's eyes, or resurrects an absent author through the gap left behind.","members":[2,6]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Praise That Misses the Point","laconic":"Critics laud surface texture, dodging the film's actual indictment.","note":"Each reading turns critical acclaim into evidence of evasion—praising grain, wordlessness, or surface becomes the very blindness the film diagnoses. The applause performs the failure.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Lotso As The Wounded Tyrant Of Abandonment","laconic":"Sunnyside's despot reads as betrayal metabolized into carceral cruelty.","note":"Each reading interprets Lotso's rule through the trauma of being discarded—abandonment hardening into bureaucratic tyranny, refused mourning, and a politics of who gets thrown away. The cluster coheres around the single code of the abandoned-one-turned-jailer.","members":[0,1,2,3,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Studio In Ruins Forced The Real Street","laconic":"Location shooting born of necessity when the soundstage no longer stood.","note":"Each reading attributes neorealist authenticity not to aesthetic choice but to material collapse — the studio in rubble, the street as the only set left. The accident of ruin becomes the alibi of realism.","members":[0,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Vietnam Bleeding Through The Genre Frame","laconic":"War's atrocity reportage smuggled into horror and fiction.","note":"Each reading insists a film's true subject is Vietnam-era war and its image culture, disguised as horror, science fiction, or crime. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Utensil That Refuses Its Category","laconic":"A misfit fork or spork becomes the threshold of selfhood and proof.","note":"Each reading fixes on a humble eating utensil that cannot be sorted into its assigned bin — garbage, toy, object — and reads that uncategorizability as the very birth of consciousness, identity, or evidence of the real. The trope is the spork/fork as the thing that refuses classification and thereby announces a self.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Self That Will Not Hold Its Image","laconic":"Identity refuses to coincide with the portrait fixed upon it.","note":"Both films stage a being whose true self resists the static image others demand it inhabit. The face and the shapeshifter alike refuse to coincide with their fixed representations.","members":[0,2]},{"name":"The Mirror That Devours Its Gazer","laconic":"Reflection turns predator, consuming the one who looks.","note":"Here the mirror is not passive surface but appetite. The act of beholding one's reflected image breeds something that hunts and consumes the beholder.","members":[1,3]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Father Reconstructed From Absence","laconic":"The child assembles a father she cannot fully know.","note":"The father is not remembered but conjured—built from longing, returning as voice, phantasm, or universal center. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Camera That Births The Image-Economy","laconic":"Photography as predatory extraction, grief monetized into circulating image.","note":"Both readings fix on the paparazzo as origin of an economy that converts private suffering into public commodity. The camera is figured not as witness but as plunderer, the founding act of an image-market.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Coach Who Plays Through Another's Body","laconic":"Barred from the court, they win by piloting a surrogate.","note":"A figure denied direct play — by injury, capital, or institution — exerts mastery vicariously through the athlete they direct. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Scan That Reveals No Lesion","laconic":"The MRI sees tissue, never the rot in the social body.","note":"Both readings treat the film's title (R.M.N., the Romanian MRI) as a diagnostic device that images flesh but cannot locate the sickness of community or soul. The scan is the central interpretive code.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Surplus Commodity As Discarded Life","laconic":"Capitalism's leftover goods become the storehouse of abandoned, unsellable, surviving lives.","note":"These readings all convert objects of overproduction — toys, canvases, dead retail stock, unsold tickets — into figures of human surplus: the unsold thing as the unwanted person. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Still Life That Names The Dead","laconic":"A title pun: the genre word becomes an epitaph for the unmourned.","note":"Both readings seize 'still life' as a death-pun, where the painterly genre of arranged inert objects becomes a figure for lives held motionless and persons outlived by their things. The code is the title-as-memento-mori.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Care Rehearsed at the Threshold of Death","laconic":"Tending the dying becomes ritual performance, not mere comfort.","note":"Each reading frames care for the dying as a staged, almost ceremonial act — birthday songs, performed tending, the body-reader who reads death. Care is theater at the deathbed.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Slaughter Staged As Beautiful Spectacle","laconic":"Mass killing rendered as gorgeous, festive, aesthetically intoxicating display.","note":"Each reading converts murder into pure aesthetic event — confetti genocide, exploding heads as fireworks, war as choreographed spectacle. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Award As Genre's Permission Slip","laconic":"Oscar recognition legitimizes performance the genre wasn't supposed to allow.","note":"Each reading treats the Academy's nod as institutional validation that decodes what the film 'meant' — rewarding the loud performance, the costume over cause, or granting the genre belated respectability. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Light That Sustains And Destroys Desire","laconic":"Lamp, flame, beacon as the screen of psychoanalytic and rational fantasy.","note":"Each reading treats a source of light (lantern, flame, lighthouse) as a semiotic device staging desire, recognition, or reason — the illuminating object as veil over the Real. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Caged Bird Is the Confined Self","laconic":"Captive songbirds as miniatures of imprisoned subjects under domestic or state control.","note":"Each reading reads a caged bird as the externalized figure of a confined human interiority — wife, worker, poet, monarch, fugitive. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Los Angeles As Counterfeit Dream-Stage","laconic":"The city of dreams revealed as a soundstage illusion.","note":"Both readings expose Los Angeles as a fabricated dreamscape, where the 'real' city is itself a performance or backlot. The trope treats LA's geography as inherently theatrical, a set pretending to be a place.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Samurai Code As Black Survival Technology","laconic":"Bushido reborn as diasporic discipline and hip-hop's looping practice.","note":"These readings fuse the warrior code with Black diasporic life — survival, sampling, the beat as bushido. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Citizen Liquidated Into Corporate Asset","laconic":"Personhood dissolved into a balance-sheet line, the human hyphen erased.","note":"Both readings cast RoboCop as the parable of a citizen converted into corporate property, the self reduced to a liquidatable, deletable asset. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Water As The Engine Of Domination","laconic":"He who controls the flow controls the people.","note":"Each reading treats hydraulic infrastructure — dam, tap, cannon — as the apparatus through which power conquers, starves, or extracts from a dependent populace.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Renunciation As Self-Defeating Virtue","laconic":"The principled withdrawal that betrays the very good it serves.","note":"Each reading treats an act of renunciation or resignation not as moral triumph but as the conscience undermining itself — abnegation disguised as, or curdling into, defeat. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Reception Reveals The Critic's Bias","laconic":"Critical responses to a 'minor' Denis film expose the reviewers' prejudices.","note":"Both readings invert the object of analysis from film to its critical reception, treating reviewers' surprise or hunger as the diagnostic symptom. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The World Emptied of Its Subject","laconic":"Films that decenter the human, leaving only flow and positions.","note":"Both readings stage a world after or without the subject—Flow's post-human animal drift and Buñuel's chain of contingent positions. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Self Authored Into Being","laconic":"A timid man wills a bolder self by naming and writing it.","note":"Each reading treats identity as performative fiction: a fabricated name or authored persona becomes the engine of self-transformation. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Music As Europe's Wounded Conscience","laconic":"Shared instruments and composers stage Europe's culture wrecked by nationalism.","note":"Each reading treats music — Mozart, Chopin, a shared instrument, absent violinists — as the body of European culture, violated or vacated by war and the nation-state. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Map That Consumes Its Territory","laconic":"Representation overtakes, erases, or kills the reality it claims to chart.","note":"Each reading stages the collision between a model (map, novel, blueprint) and the lived territory it abstracts — the sign devouring or marking its referent. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Viewer's Recoil Is The Verdict","laconic":"Audience discomfort reframed as confession, not critique.","note":"Each reading turns the spectator's unease into the real subject—our flinching diagnoses our own bigotry, disavowal, or symptomatic squeamishness rather than the film's flaw.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Loud Guide Who Knows Nothing","laconic":"Meek's confident bluster masks ignorance, terror, and imperial fraud.","note":"All three read Meek as the swaggering authority whose performed certainty is hollow — a bluff dressed as command, leading the lost deeper into wilderness. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Ringing That Unmakes The Self","laconic":"Tinnitus and ringing as the audible erosion of identity.","note":"Across these readings, the high-pitched ring is never mere physiological damage but the sound of a self coming apart — grief, dissolution, the real breaking through. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Tyrant Played As Clown","laconic":"Comedy strips the dictator of terror by making him absurd.","note":"These readings all stage the despot deflated through buffoonery, mime, or imagined caricature — Chaplin's dancing dictator haunts the whole set. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Praise For 'Gentleness' As Critical Symptom","laconic":"Reviewers' love of gentleness reads as a confession of their own hunger.","note":"Each reading treats critical acclaim for a film's 'gentleness' not as description but as diagnosis — the praise exposes what critics crave or lack. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Tyranny Of The Maxim","laconic":"A governing rule recoils on those who enforce it.","note":"Both readings frame a self-imposed universal principle that becomes a cage, turning moral certainty into the very mechanism of its undoing. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Akira As The Absent Cosmogonic God","laconic":"The named one is no boy but an unborn universe.","note":"Both readings refuse Akira-as-character, recasting the name as a generative cosmic principle—an absent deity around which order is built. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Healer Who Took Up the Sword","laconic":"The physician who abandons medicine for revolt or rot.","note":"Each reading turns the doctor-figure into a political actor: diagnosis becomes militancy, healing becomes contagion or insurgency. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Withdrawn Author Who Authors By Withdrawing","laconic":"Kiarostami's method as the visible absence of its maker.","note":"Both readings locate the film's truth in the director's self-erasure—the diminutive car glimpsed at a distance, the unmanned dashboard camera—where method becomes meaning precisely by removing the hand that shapes it.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Painter Who Films Without Words","laconic":"Korean auteur framed as silent painter rather than dramatist.","note":"These readings recast the director's compositions as a painter's eye, prizing wordless image over screenwriterly dialogue. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Vanished City Rebuilt As Memory","laconic":"Lost urban places reconstructed as elegy for what no longer exists.","note":"Each reading treats a film's setting as a deliberate reconstruction of a place erased by time, mourning a vanished commons. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Casting As The Argument It Stages","laconic":"Recasting and recognition become the film's own thesis made flesh.","note":"These readings treat the casting apparatus itself—recast faces, recast ensembles, faces that fail to be recognized—as the carrier of meaning, not merely a production fact. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Iberian Coast As Buried Otherness","laconic":"Atlantic and Mediterranean shores stage what the nation cannot archive.","note":"Each reading converts a stretch of Iberian coastline into a repository for the repressed — a Persia that stayed, an Atlantic unconscious, an archive's antidote. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Fade To Black As Mortal Punctuation","laconic":"Editing's blackouts read as the film's own dying heartbeat.","note":"Each reading treats the fade or blackout not as transition but as a temporal wound — death, grief, or memory's failure inscribed in the cut itself. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Festival That Frees What Order Suppressed","laconic":"Ritual celebration unleashes the body, the repressed, the briefly empowered.","note":"Each reading treats the festival as a sanctioned eruption — a carnival or purification that surfaces what social order represses rather than cleansing it. {"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Caregiver Whose Love Is A Cage","laconic":"Healing becomes captivity; the wound is the bond.","note":"The nurse and the lover both administer care as control, refusing the cure that would end the dependency. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Saul's Loyalty As Anti-Market Devotion","laconic":"The dealer who chooses attachment over profit and survival.","note":"Both readings cast Saul's devotion as a refusal of transactional logic — loyalty as displaced object-attachment that defies the market's demand for self-interest.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Glass That Hides Instead Of Reveals","laconic":"Transparency weaponized as concealment; the see-through surface that conceals all.","note":"These readings share a single semiotic move: glass/transparency that promises disclosure but delivers obfuscation, surveillance, or pure surface. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Stolen Voice That Names Him","laconic":"Borrowed art as confession of an unformed, plagiarized self.","note":"Both readings hinge on appropriation as identity: the boy claims another's song/words, and the theft itself becomes the truest self-portrait. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Outsider Band Forging Itself","laconic":"Misfit children become a self-made republic, not a bloodline.","note":"Both readings recast The Goonies as a chosen fellowship—identity and belonging willed into being rather than handed down. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Game Surrenders To The Spreadsheet","laconic":"Quantification displaces intuition, recasting the sport as a managed ledger.","note":"These readings converge on the moment data colonizes baseball — the spreadsheet as the instrument that disciplines labor and dissolves the game into numbers. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Score That Diagnoses The Film","laconic":"Music chosen not to accompany but to render psyche or system.","note":"Each reading treats the score as the film's hidden thesis—Brötzmann's scream for the architect, synth loops for the savant mind, machine-music for industrial war. The instrumentation IS the interpretation.","members":[0,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Stripper Who Builds Furniture","laconic":"Mike's craftsmanship as counter-identity to his commodified flesh.","note":"Both readings fix on Mike's furniture-making as the trope of the objectified body asserting a self through making solid, owned objects. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Teacher As Screen For Projected Desire","laconic":"Pupil's longing renders the teacher object, not person.","note":"Each reading positions the teacher not as a subject but as a surface onto which desire, dream, or fantasy is projected and then disavowed. {"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Director Who Built What He Mocked","laconic":"The auteur engineers the very modernity his film satirizes.","note":"Both readings of Playtime locate Tati as the maker who constructs the sterile machine-world he ridicules, satirist as architect.","members":[1,2]},{"name":"The Self-Destroying Machine At Full Speed","laconic":"Set-pieces as elaborate apparatus engineered to spectacularly fail.","note":"Both invoke the Tinguely-style contraption: a glorious mechanism whose whole point is its own breakdown and demolition in motion.","members":[3,4]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"Success Is The True Opponent In The Ring","laconic":"The real enemy is comfort, fame, the soft life after winning.","note":"Rocky III readings that relocate the antagonist from the challenger to the corrosive success the hero must un-learn. Clubber is merely the mask of complacency.","members":[3,4,5]},{"name":"The Inarticulate Fighter Whose Body Speaks His Truth","laconic":"He cannot say it; the punching is the confession.","note":"The boxer who lacks language and lets violence or silence stand as his only honest utterance. Inarticulacy is not a flaw but the truth itself.","members":[0,2,6]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Face That Forbids The Kill","laconic":"Levinas's Other: the human face commanding 'thou shalt not kill' before ideology.","note":"A tight cluster of Levinasian readings where the encountered face — of enemy, stranger, hostage, victim — issues an ethical injunction that precedes and overrides political or moral abstraction. The recurring 'forbids/commands/before ideology' phrasing makes this a single sharply-coded interpretive move.","members":[0,1,2,4,7,9]},{"name":"The Persecutor Who Becomes Penitent","laconic":"The agent of cruelty converts into the one who answers the Other.","note":"Here the loaded device is the inversion: the inflicter of violence — eavesdropper, filmmaker, trampling priest — discovers in his cruelty a duty, confession, or higher holiness toward those he wrongs.","members":[5,6,8]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Infinity As The Name Without An Exit","laconic":"Titles invoke the infinite as a prison, not a promise.","note":"Each reading converts 'infinity/mugen/無間' from grandeur into entrapment — the endless as that which has no outside, no interval, no escape. The code is the boundless rebranded as the inescapable.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"This Place Standing In For That Frontier","laconic":"One geography doubled for another mythic West.","note":"A tight code: the location-substitution reading, where a real place wears the disguise of an imagined or vanished frontier. The disguise itself carries the meaning.","members":[5,6,7,8,9,10,11,15,16,17]},{"name":"The Painter Who Raced The Frontier's Extinction","laconic":"Landscape framed as canvas chasing a vanishing world.","note":"Readings that treat the Western landscape as painted artifact — prairie-as-canvas, the painter racing extinction, the postcard already composed.","members":[2,3,12,13]},{"name":"The Frontier Promise Turned To Rot","laconic":"The cleared ledger, the imagined sentinel, the inheritance gone foul.","note":"The myth's moral residue read as anxiety, ledger, or decay — the frontier as inheritance soured rather than as filmed disguise.","members":[0,1,4,19]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Two Strands That Are One Self","laconic":"Split narratives revealed as a single divided soul or gaze.","note":"Each reading collapses an apparent doubling—two stories, two friends, two strands—into one fractured consciousness or dying perception. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Editing That Becomes the Author","laconic":"When montage, not light, writes the film's meaning.","note":"Each reading elevates a formal technique—slit-scan, dissolve, fugal cutting, the long track—into the work's true authoring force, making time and editing the source of meaning rather than the photographed image. The device stops being a tool and becomes the argument.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Face As Confessional Surface","laconic":"Olivia Colman's face becomes the film's interrogated text.","note":"Both readings treat the actress's face under directorial scrutiny as a surface where guilt is exposed and read. The shooting/being-shot pun and the confessional skin converge on the same code: filming a woman as testimony.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Tropical Paradise Filmed As Dread","laconic":"Island idyll inverted into prison, sunset, or radioactive twilight.","note":"Each reading reads the postcard paradise against its grain, finding confinement, imperial decline, or apocalyptic glow where tourism promises bliss. The lush tropical setting becomes a code for menace and exhaustion rather than escape.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Absence That Founds The Whole","laconic":"What is missing organizes everything that remains.","note":"Each reading locates the film's structuring principle in a void—a vanished person, an undefined role, a disappearance—arguing that the gap is not a mystery to solve but the answer itself.","members":[1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Self Mourned By Its Unknowing Twin","laconic":"A doubled life grieves a death it cannot name.","note":"Each reading orbits the same code: a survivor-self warned and shadowed by the death of an unmet double. The grief, the backward glance, and the unnameable warning are all facets of one mournful telepathy.","members":[0,1,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Psychic As Final Verdict","laconic":"Closing on the seer makes counsel itself the film's open ending.","note":"Both readings fix on the same terminal gesture: the psychic encounter as the film's last word, treating divination not as content but as a formal verdict on uncertainty. The recurrence of this exact device across both lines marks it as a genuine code, not a theme.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Jigsaw As Perverse Philosopher Of Worthy Survival","laconic":"The trap-master reframed as ideologue who only the deserving live.","note":"Both readings convert Jigsaw from slasher villain into a doctrinaire moralist of survival — neoliberal meritocracy and inverted Frankl alike cast his games as a philosophy that sorts the deserving from the doomed.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Single Cipher That Unlocks Everything","laconic":"One key, code, or solution decrypts the whole machine.","note":"Each reading nominates a lone decisive device — a prime, a refresh, a lobotomy, a solving mind — as the master key that resolves the entire system. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Title Cry Reattributed To Her","laconic":"His silent wandering reframed as her unvoiced anguish.","note":"Both readings wrest the film's emotional core away from the male drifter and relocate it in the woman he leaves — the withheld trauma and the misowned 'cry' are the same interpretive theft.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Advocate Who Loses to the System","laconic":"Dax defends men inside a machine that has already decided.","note":"Both readings center Colonel Dax as principled counsel pitted against an institution indifferent to justice; one frames him as savior, the other as doomed by moral mismatch. Together they form a single code: righteous argument crashing against entrenched, consequentialist power.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Ruin That Erased Its Own Ruin","laconic":"Postwar European sites filmed where erasure itself becomes the subject.","note":"Each reading locates a location whose history of destruction or imperial collapse is paved over, rebuilt, or made unfindable — the film catching the architecture in the act of erasing its own past. The trope is not 'ruins' but the doubled erasure: the place that hides the wound it carries.","members":[0,1,2,3,4,5]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Servant Who Secretly Runs The House","laconic":"The subordinate who actually holds the master's world together.","note":"Each reading inverts the master-servant hierarchy: the underling — butler, valet, maid, infiltrator, assistant — is revealed as the true engine of the plot or the load-bearing class. Borgman's caste indistinguishable from masters and the strike that exposes who holds the room belong to the same insurrectionary code.","members":[0,1,2,3,4,5]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"Verse Surviving The Dissolving Self","laconic":"Poetry persists as habit when memory and body fail.","note":"The self erodes but recitation continues — language as the last bodily reflex outliving identity. Both Eternal Memory readings render speech as residue of a vanished person.","members":[0,1]},{"name":"Poetry As The Logic-Defeating Axiom","laconic":"Verse names what reason cannot prove or contain.","note":"Poetry is wielded against the dissolving body or the tyranny of logic — an unprovable truth that outlasts what should erase it.","members":[2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Housing Block As Dying Collectivist Dream","laconic":"Kieślowski's concrete estates read as the carcass of socialist utopia.","note":"Both readings transmute the Warsaw apartment bloc into a political body — the shared estate as the failed, expiring promise of collective life. The architecture itself becomes the corpse of late socialism.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Stain That Resists All Meaning","laconic":"A bloodied object intrudes as the Real, unsymbolizable.","note":"Both readings name a literal blood-marked object as the Lacanian Real—the traumatic residue that no symbolic order can absorb. The device and its meaning are identical across both.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Quest That Veils The Real","laconic":"Every quest masks an encounter with death or the unstaged Real.","note":"Each reading treats the ostensible journey as a screen for a confrontation with mortality or authenticity, the symbolic game concealing the Real. The shared move is the quest-as-veil, not the quest itself.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Score And Take That Refuse The Cut","laconic":"Unbroken continuity weaponized against editing's severance of feeling.","note":"Both readings cast a sustained device — score in one, the long take in the other — as a defiance of montage's fragmentation, an insistence on continuous emotional and bodily presence.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Score Withheld As Argument","laconic":"Absent or refused music becomes a deliberate aesthetic and moral stance.","note":"These readings treat the soundtrack's absence or refusal as a polemic — against streaming's background-noise economy, against easy interiority. The Challengers entry inverts the move (a score that refuses to recede) but belongs to the same code: scoring as contested terrain.","members":[0,1,2,3,4,5]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Outsider Who Survives By Not Belonging","laconic":"Non-membership becomes the only safe position when the group turns lethal.","note":"Each reading inverts the usual penalty for being the outsider: detachment, marginality, or non-participation is precisely what spares or vindicates the figure the in-group would otherwise destroy. The group's logic of belonging is recast as a death-trap that the outsider escapes by never having entered.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Film Written Each Morning On Set","laconic":"Scriptless, daily improvisation as the film's generative structure","note":"Both readings locate the work's form in Hong Sang-soo's method of composing scenes the morning of shooting, making process itself the structuring principle.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Collector Hoarding A World Out Of Reach","laconic":"Protagonists who curate artifacts of a life they cannot inhabit.","note":"Each figure compulsively gathers and preserves objects as proxies for a vanished or forbidden existence — the collection stands in for the living they're denied. WALL·E, Ariel, and Andy share the curator's longing; the prospector's reclusive real-estate hoarding is a thinner fit but rides the same code.","members":[0,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Censor's Hand Became the Style","laconic":"State restriction forged the very aesthetic — children, ellipses, costumes, doorways.","note":"These readings share one strong move: Iranian cinema's constraints under theocracy are recast not as limits but as generative formal devices. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Grammar As The Film's True Tense","laconic":"The film conjugates a verb mood rather than telling a story.","note":"Each reading insists the film's form is a grammatical mood or tense — boyhood as duration, childhood and ambition as subjunctive possibility — privileging conjugation over plot. The code reads cinema as grammar made visible.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Devil Wears A Borrowed Face","laconic":"Evil disguises itself as the disavowed, the angelic, the vanished.","note":"Each reading locates the demonic not as an open antagonist but as a hidden engine wearing a benign or feminine mask. The devil's power is its concealment — desire in drag, an angel's shell, a disappearing trick.","members":[0,3]},{"name":"The Vanishing As The Whole Trick","laconic":"The disappearance, not the appearance, is the film's true method.","note":"These readings argue the work's entire structure is built on an absence — the devil who vanishes is the device itself.","members":[2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Anonymous Tape As Externalized Conscience","laconic":"Unattributed recordings arrive as accusation, surveillance becomes the judging superego.","note":"The recurring move: a tape with no visible author returns to indict its subject, the medium standing in for conscience or the return of the repressed. Lost Highway, Caché, MaXXXine, and the smuggled VHS of Dogtooth all weaponize footage as a verdict from outside.","members":[0,1,2,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Servant Whose Worship Conceals Forbidden Desire","laconic":"Loyalty curdles into love that dares not name itself.","note":"Two readings cast the obsessive female devotee as harboring a desire disavowed as hatred or mourning. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Zigzag Hill Path As Kiarostami's Signature","laconic":"The switchback road etched into earth becomes the auteur's recurring glyph.","note":"The serpentine hill path recurs across the Koker films as a visible mark of authorship and the shape of return. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Dawn As The Title's Secret Resurrection","laconic":"A word for sunrise renamed as the rebirth of something else.","note":"Each reading seizes a title-word — dawn, sunrise, resurrection — and insists it names not literal daybreak but the death or return of an order: of images, of a soul, of a dream, of an economy. {"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Robber Who Holds A Kantian Maxim","laconic":"Robbery enacted as a moral law, not mere theft.","note":"Two readings recode the bank robber as a Kantian agent — the crime executed by categorical imperative or as a failed universalizable principle of love.","members":[1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Queer Man Who Speaks Through Silence","laconic":"Inarticulate masculinity loving in a language that cannot be spoken.","note":"Each reading frames same-sex desire as an unutterable code routed through landscape, body, and labor rather than confession. The recurring move: emotion that survives precisely because it refuses speech.","members":[0,1,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Critics Who Convicted Themselves","laconic":"Each reading turns reception into a re-enactment of the film's own gesture.","note":"All three readings indict criticism itself: the act of interpreting the female protagonist replays the film's central violence or demand for meaning. The critic becomes complicit, not observer.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Voice-Over Spoken From Beyond The Grave","laconic":"Narration as the testimony of the already-dead.","note":"The voice-over is decoupled from a living present, sounding instead like a man narrating his own foregone death. The grain of the voice exceeds its words.","members":[1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Obsolescence as a Mode of Being","laconic":"The film's true subject is the master outrun by his world.","note":"Each reading locates the film's ontology in the obsolete — a craft, a genre, a man, a commodity — outpaced by a world that no longer needs it. The strikingness is that obsolescence is not lamented but treated as a way of existing.","members":[0,1,2,3,4,5]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Long Take As A Withheld Cut","laconic":"The unbroken shot reads as a refusal, a manufacturing of meaning.","note":"Each reading treats the long take not as style but as a semiotic refusal — to cut away, to consume, to relieve risk. The withheld edit becomes the loaded device.","members":[0,2,3]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Tape That Plays Its Listener","laconic":"Recorded media stops being information and becomes the haunting itself.","note":"Both films treat the tape as a surface onto which the audience projects dread, guilt, or doom — the recording's true content is the receiver's own undoing, not any neutral signal.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Crime Restaged On Its Own Soil","laconic":"A nation's guilt filmed in the very place it haunts.","note":"Each reading binds a film's setting or production geography to a buried national crime, reading the location itself as the return of a repressed historical guilt. The strikingness is the displacement: shooting or staging atrocity precisely where (or where it cannot be admitted) it occurred.","members":[0,1,3,4]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The One Who Renounced Their Gift as Vocation","laconic":"Renunciation reframed not as loss but as a chosen, sacred calling.","note":"Each reading recasts withdrawal — from speech, from the world, from the track — as an affirmative doctrine rather than defeat. The trope's charge is that abstention itself becomes the higher devotion.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Employee Erased Without Being Fired","laconic":"Management dissolves a worker through silence rather than dismissal.","note":"Both readings fix on Milton as the man never officially terminated, only made to disappear through neglect and plausible deniability. {"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Audience That Cannot Bear Ambiguity","laconic":"The critic's hunt for the 'real' answer is a positivist flinch.","note":"Both readings indict the interpretive reflex that demands a single resolved truth from films built on irresolvable doubling. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Place Forged On A Foreign Stage","laconic":"A locale conjured wholesale on a soundstage that is elsewhere.","note":"Each reading insists the depicted place is an artifice manufactured in another country's studio, the geography existing only as fabrication. The trope activates the expectation that the 'real' setting is a deliberate, displaced theatrical construction.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Palette Disciplined Against Its Own Excess","laconic":"Critics read restraint as a director caging his native color.","note":"These readings share one code: stylistic restraint interpreted as self-discipline, the auteur reining in a signature excess of color or melodrama. The recurring move treats subtraction as the meaningful act and reads critical praise of 'restraint' as bias against maximalism.","members":[0,1,2,4,5,6]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"The Rats As Plague's Repressed Return","laconic":"Vermin embody history's buried catastrophe made flesh.","note":"Both readings treat Herzog's rats as more than set dressing — a swarm carrying the return of plague-history, whether as repressed catastrophe or via eleven thousand literal bodies.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Ellipsis As Secret Editing Grammar","laconic":"What goes unshown carries the film's true meaning.","note":"These readings locate each film's power in the gap, the cut, the unsaid — the ellipsis elevated from punctuation to method. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Seam Where Archive Becomes Living Footage","laconic":"The visible splice fuses real document to staged fiction, reviving the dead.","note":"Each reading locates meaning in the seam itself — the edit where historical footage meets fabricated image, resurrecting the past as continuous film. The 'mended seam' as restoration is the same move applied to the medium's own body.","members":[0,1,2]}]}

{"verdict":"multi","groups":[{"name":"Inspiration As Theft From The Dead","laconic":"The poet's muse is stolen voices of the deceased.","note":"Both readings recast Orpheus's creative reception as a transgressive feeding on the dead, the artist eavesdropping where he should not. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"Electra As Keeper Of National Mourning","laconic":"The grieving daughter incarnates a nation's unburied historical loss.","note":"Both readings recast the Electra figure as the bearer of collective melancholy—mourning a lost father who stands in for the Greek catastrophe itself. The mythic and the historical fuse in her endurance.","members":[0,1]}]}

{"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Master-Slave Dialectic Run For Recognition","laconic":"Hegelian bondage: servitude, mastery, and the mutual struggle for recognition.","note":"Each reading stages the Hegelian master-slave dialectic—domination, servile self-policing, and the demand for recognition that binds master to slave. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Cut As Statement, Not Stitch","laconic":"Editing read as meaning-bearing utterance, deliberately rupturing continuity.","note":"Each reading treats the cut not as invisible craft but as an authored speech act — a deliberate severance that carries trauma, wish, or refusal. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Pacific Northwest As Liquid Dread","laconic":"Perpetual rain reads the region as a soggy emotional purgatory.","note":"Both readings treat the saturated Northwest climate as an externalized mood-machine, the rain itself doing the affective and ominous work. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The One Who Refuses As Kantian Duty","laconic":"Refusal framed as moral law against consequence and the state.","note":"Each reading recasts a refusal as Kantian principle — conscience holding firm against the tyrant, the state, or mere outcome. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Actress Cast As Her Own Mother","laconic":"Performance collapses the daughter into the maternal role she replays.","note":"Each reading stages a woman compelled to re-enact, devour, or re-author a maternal figure through performance—identity dissolving into the mother she plays. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Children's Film That Wounds On Purpose","laconic":"Family entertainment whose cruelty is the point, not the betrayal.","note":"These readings treat ostensibly child-friendly films as deliberate dispensers of trauma, where wholesomeness and reverence are vehicles for cruelty inflicted on young audiences. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Lens That Dethrones Its Subject","laconic":"Optical distortion strips authority, refusing the commanding view.","note":"Both readings treat lens distortion as a deliberate refusal to grant mastery—rendering a king as patient, a man denied God's-eye certainty. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Surname As Inherited Creed","laconic":"A father's name becomes a belief one must reckon with, unchosen.","note":"All three read 'Creed' as the pun it dares you to ignore — a surname that doubles as an article of faith, an inheritance of belief rather than blood. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Peace That Is War Renamed","laconic":"'Peace' as war's continuation, exception, or catastrophe under another name.","note":"Each reading inverts the armistice: the ceasefire is not war's end but its perpetuation by other means — a Clausewitzian formula run backwards. {"verdict":"code","groups":[{"name":"The Christian Father As Defeated Japan","laconic":"Faith-bound paternity read as the nation's wounded, submissive psyche.","note":"Both readings of Imamura's film map the Catholic father onto a defeated Imperial Japan, his submission a national wound rooted in Kyushu's hidden-Christian coast.
